docs.title: ollamarun
docs.text:
A terminal agent harness for Ollama — a personal project about how far local models go when you hand them tools.

ollamarun began as a nicer ollama run: streamed markdown, 2D Unicode math, sessions that actually persist. It has since grown into a full harness — an approval-gated tool loop, two front ends, remote inference, context/GPU placement fitting, and an HTTP API layer (ollamarun serve) that speaks both the OpenAI API and its own native agent API.

Every ollama run flag (ollama 0.34) is accepted and extended, so it still doubles as a drop-in replacement for the CLI it started as.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
Needs Linux, Python 3.10+ and a reachable Ollama server (default 127.0.0.1:11434).

$ pip install --user rich requests prompt_toolkit
$ ./ollamarun qwen3:8b "explain this repo"    # one-shot
$ ./ollamarun qwen3:8b                        # interactive REPL

docs.title: Status
docs.text:
Early, single-developer and moving. Built against one Linux box and a small Tailscale fleet; Python 3.10; a few tools are wired to my own side projects and degrade gracefully when those are absent. Rough edges are part of the deal — expect the structure to keep changing as the learning continues.

More background in Project overview; Apache-2.0 · Acknowledgements.

docs.title: API overview
docs.text:
ollamarun serve puts an HTTP API in front of Ollama from the same process that runs the CLI. Two surfaces share the listener:

  • the OpenAI API — GET /v1/models, POST /v1/chat/completions, POST /v1/embeddings: model turns only, a stateless translation proxy any OpenAI client can talk to;
  • the native agent API — full agent turns with the tool loop, approvals, sessions, artifacts and context fits.
$ ollamarun serve [--bind IP] [--port N] [--host HOST | --remote NAME] [--keep-loaded]

Starting it prints what is in force — the real banner from a --port 0 run:

ollamarun serve · 2.0 · OpenAI-compatible + agent API
  listening http://0.0.0.0:38573 (all interfaces)
  upstream  http://127.0.0.1:11434
  workspace /home/you/code/ollamarun
  models /v1/models · chat /v1/chat/completions · agent turns /v1/agent/turns ·
sessions /v1/sessions
trusted-network-only: no authentication — never expose this port to the internet
Ctrl-C stops the server (active turns are cancelled; loaded models are kept)

--bind/--port choose the listener (port 0 picks an ephemeral one); --host/--remote pick the Ollama machine; the two are independent. The workspace line is the tool jail.

Trusted-network-only

The service has no authentication, and the bind address is its only boundary. Keep it on the LAN/tailnet and never expose the port to the public internet.

docs.title: Lifecycle
docs.text:
Disconnects. A dropped event stream is an unsubscribe, not a cancellation — the turn keeps running and its results land in the session. Both sides of that were checked live:

--- default: turn_ef28e7b2a20d
  client dropped the stream: ConnectionError
  status after disconnect: completed (checked 8s)
--- cancel_on_disconnect: turn_9ac3c55775b0
  client dropped the stream: ConnectionError
  status after disconnect: cancelled (checked 2s)

A turn that asks for "cancel_on_disconnect": true cancels when its stream drops; otherwise it finishes. POST /v1/agent/turns/{id}/cancel is the explicit path — it aborts the in-flight generation, kills cancellable subprocesses, resolves a parked approval as cancelled and persists the terminal state.

Shutdown is ordered: the listener stops accepting, new turns and fits are refused (503 server_shutting_down), parked approvals resolve as cancelled, in-flight HTTP handlers drain within serve_shutdown_timeout, and serve_unload_on_exit (default true) unloads only the models this server actually used — embedding models stay resident and a parallel CLI session's models are never touched (--keep-loaded disables it).

docs.title: Everything the API can be
docs.text:
Knob Effect serve_agent: false Inference + files only; the native routes are not registered (404). The banner says agent routes disabled. serve_models: ["qwen3*"] An allowlist; a model outside it answers exactly like an unknown one (404 model_not_found) everywhere — list, lookup, chat, sessions, turns, fits. serve_workspace: DIR The tool path jail (default: the directory serve started in). serve_fit: off\|estimate\|probe Gates the fit surface.

Both switches were exercised live: with serve_agent: false and serve_models: ["qwen3*"], the model list showed only the qwen3 entries, llama3.2:3b answered 404 model_not_found, POST /v1/agent/turns was 404 unknown endpoint, and POST /v1/files still answered 201. Details on Security and limits.

docs.text:

docs.title: Example clients
docs.text: Two reference clients under examples/ double as integration checks against a running ollamarun serve. Both print a PASS/SKIP/FAIL line per step and exit non-zero when a step fails.

docs.title: examples/openai_client.py
docs.text:
The official openai SDK against the /v1 surface: the model list, a non-streaming completion, streaming with usage, embeddings, n = 2, and a tools request that the server must accept without executing. Run against a chat model:

$ python3 examples/openai_client.py --base-url http://127.0.0.1:38573/v1 --model llama3.2:3b
openai_client · SDK 2.29.0 · http://127.0.0.1:38573/v1
PASS  the model list answers
      using model llama3.2:3b
PASS  a non-streaming completion returns content and usage
PASS  streaming deltas arrive and usage closes the stream
SKIP  embeddings return one vector per input — llama3.2:3b is not an embedding model
PASS  n=2 returns two indexed choices
PASS  a tools request is accepted (the server never executes it)
      the model asked for get_weather({"city": "Sao Paulo"})

all checks passed

The embeddings step needs an embedding model, so a chat-model run reports SKIP there — by design. Point it at an embedding model to exercise that step; the chat steps then fail with the sanitized backend 502 (an embedding model cannot chat), which is the expected outcome of that trade:

$ python3 examples/openai_client.py --base-url … --model nomic-embed-text
PASS  embeddings return one vector per input
FAIL  a non-streaming completion returns content and usage
      InternalServerError("Error code: 502 - {'error': {'message': 'the model
      backend failed to complete the request', …}}")

Options: --base-url (the /v1 suffix included), --model (defaults to the first listed), --api-key (sent and ignored), --timeout.

docs.title: examples/agent_client.py
docs.text:
The native agent flow over plain HTTP: submit a turn, follow the typed event stream, resolve a parked approval, print the session summary. The default policy mode runs allowlisted/read-only tools and denies the rest:

$ python3 examples/agent_client.py --base-url http://127.0.0.1:38573 \
      --model llama3.2:3b --prompt "List the files in the current directory and tell me how many there are."
turn turn_07f31de8504b · session 20261018-133348-fc8d · model llama3.2:3b · approval policy
tool · list_dir {"path": "."}
  → ok ['/tmp/…/serve-ws (2 entries)']
There are 2 files in the current directory.
status completed · rounds 1 · tokens 642
answer There are 2 files in the current directory.

--mode interactive --approve run exercises the approval path (the client parks, prints the decision request, posts the decision, and continues):

$ python3 examples/agent_client.py --base-url … --model llama3.2:3b \
      --mode interactive --approve run \
      --prompt "Use write_file to write the text from-the-client to client-demo.txt, then confirm."
turn turn_459cb29e505b · session 20261018-133515-cdb4 · model llama3.2:3b · approval interactive
tool · write_file {"append": false, "content": "from-the-client", "path": "client-demo.txt"}
approval required write_file modifies state
      resolved as run (200)
  → ok ['wrote 15 chars to /tmp/…/serve-ws/client-demo.txt']

(The file really was written — checked on disk afterwards.) Other options: --session-id to continue an existing session instead of creating one, --approve {run,remember,rule,auto,deny}, --no-persist for an ephemeral turn, --json for machine output, --timeout.

Both clients are covered by the test suite (test_examples, against a fake stack), so they cannot rot silently — and they are the shortest way to check a live deployment by hand.

docs.title: Security and limits
docs.text:
Trusted-network-only

The service has no authentication, and the bind address is its only boundary. Keep it on the LAN/tailnet and never expose the port to the public internet.

docs.title: Deployment and auth
docs.text: ollamarun serve is meant to run on the trusted network under the user's own service management (the serve_* keys cover the listener, limits and shutdown; the startup banner prints the surface in effect). There is deliberately no authentication yet — the bind address is the only boundary. When authentication lands it wraps these routes without reshaping them: it is a transport concern, and never a substitute for the tool-approval gate.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
The JSON body cap is serve_body_limit (default 32 MiB), and it applies to Content-Length and chunked bodies alike: a chunked upload is decoded with the cumulative decoded size checked before each chunk is read, Transfer-Encoding together with Content-Length is an ambiguity error, and malformed framing (bad sizes, missing CRLF, truncation, a missing terminal chunk, a non-chunked coding) is a structured 400.

Resolving content parts is bounded separately, because a small body can name many large inputs: serve_max_messages, serve_max_content_parts, serve_max_message_bytes, serve_max_text_bytes, serve_max_images and serve_max_image_bytes (cumulative after resolving data URIs, remote fetches and file inlines; counts fail before any fetch). Embeddings inputs are charged to the same budget (input count, per-input bytes, total text). Violations are 413 input_too_large naming the limit.

serve_request_timeout (default 30 s) is a per-operation socket timeout — a streaming response that keeps writing (heartbeats included) is never cut off by it — and serve_sse_ping_interval (default 15 s) is the SSE heartbeat.

docs.title: Model allowlist
docs.text:
serve_models (default: empty) restricts which models the API exposes and accepts: names or fnmatch patterns matched against the installed models after tag normalization (qwen3 matches qwen3:latest; qwen3* matches every tag). The list applies everywhere a model is selected, listed or used — the model list, lookup, chat completions, session creation and model edits, agent turns (a stored session whose model fell out of the list is refused before it runs) and the fit endpoints — and a model outside it answers exactly like an unknown one (404 model_not_found).

Checked live with serve_models: ["qwen3*"]:

$ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:PORT/v1/models | …                 # only qwen3* entries
$ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:PORT/v1/models/llama3.2:3b
{"error": {"message": "model 'llama3.2:3b' not found", "type": "invalid_request_error",
 "param": "model", "code": "model_not_found"}}          # HTTP 404

docs.title: Tool workspace
docs.text:
Serve runs its tool context jailed to serve_workspace (default: the directory serve started in, printed in the banner): relative paths in the file tools resolve under it, resolved escapes — symlinks included — are refused, and the run_shell/run_python working directories follow the same rule. A model asking for a path outside gets a refusal as the tool result:

tool · list_dir {"path": "/tmp"}
  → error ['refused: /tmp is outside the workspace root (/home/you/serve-dir)']

This is an argument and default-working-directory policy, not subprocess confinement: an approved command can still reach whatever the process user can. The CLI keeps its previous behavior.

docs.title: Feature switches
docs.text:
serve_agent: false runs the process as an inference server: the native routes (turns, approvals, sessions, fits) are not registered at all, while models, chat completions and the /v1/files + /v1/artifacts/* endpoints keep serving — the OpenAI surface can still send file parts. The banner spells it out (files /v1/files (agent routes disabled)), and the refusal is a plain 404:

$ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:PORT/v1/agent/turns -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{…}'
{"error": {"message": "unknown endpoint: POST /v1/agent/turns",
 "type": "invalid_request_error", "param": null, "code": "not_found"}}   # HTTP 404

One model policy applies to every route: see the allowlist above.

Every key with its default, range and zero semantics is listed in Config file.

docs.title: Approvals
docs.text:
settings.approval decides who answers a tool call:

  • "policy" (the default) applies the configured tool policy — allowlisted and rule-covered calls run, everything else is denied with a note. The serve policy is never auto; --yes remains the only CLI auto path.
  • "interactive" parks genuinely undecided calls: the turn enters waiting_approval and emits approval.required with the approval_id, the call, the reason and suggested rules.

docs.title: The parked event
docs.text:
A real capture (write_file in interactive mode):

{
  "name": "write_file",
  "args": {"path": "approve-demo.txt", "append": false, "content": "approved-by-api"},
  "detail": "approve-demo.txt (15 chars)",
  "fingerprint": "write_file:{\"append\": false, \"content\": \"approved-by-api\", \"path\": \"approve-demo.txt\"}",
  "reason": "write_file modifies state",
  "suggestions": [
    {"kind": "path", "pattern": "approve-demo.txt", "base": "/home/you/serve-dir", "created": "…"},
    {"kind": "path", "pattern": "**", "base": "/home/you/serve-dir", "created": "…"}
  ],
  "approval_id": "apr_83764cec6535"
}

The park is preceded on the same stream by tool.call (the call panel equivalent) and followed, on decision, by approval.resolved. The suggestions are the same generalized rules the CLI offers; the fingerprint powers "remember exactly this call".

docs.title: Deciding
docs.text:
POST /v1/agent/approvals/{id} — the first decision wins; duplicates get 409.

Request body Effect {"action": "run"} Run this call once. {"action": "remember"} Run it, remembering the exact call for the session. {"action": "rule", "rule": {"kind": "path", "pattern": "reports/**"}} Run it and store a generalized rule (call, shell, path or python). {"action": "auto"} Allow everything for the rest of this turn. {"action": "deny"} Refuse it; the model gets a not-run note. 
$ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:11440/v1/agent/approvals/apr_83764cec6535 \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"action": "run"}'
{"id": "apr_83764cec6535", "object": "approval", "turn_id": "turn_7cc9871fcf7d",
 "action": "run", "run": true, "note": "confirmed",
 "resolved_at": "2026-10-18T13:20:09.745442-03:00"}

After run, the same turn went on to tool.result (ok), published the written file as an artifact and completed with the model's confirmation. After deny:

{"id": "apr_783809fe4258", "object": "approval", "turn_id": "turn_82bf7ce2fbc2",
 "action": "deny", "run": false, "note": "denied by the user", "resolved_at": "…"}

…the tool result is a not-run note and the file is not written (checked on disk). The model still answered in that run — models sometimes claim success anyway; the harness's record (tool.result, the session) shows what actually happened, which is why clients should decide from events, not prose.

docs.title: Timeouts and edge cases
docs.text:
• An unanswered approval times out (serve_approval_timeout, default 300 s) as denied: the tool result says not run: approval timed out and the model continues.
  • A turn cancelled or shut down while parked resolves the approval as cancelled (200 with the resolved state), so clients never hang.
  • The decision endpoint is per-approval; there is no bulk form — auto is the per-turn escalation.

The rules engine behind the decisions is the CLI's — see Approvals and policy for kinds, matching and the floor no rule can cover.

docs.title: Artifacts
docs.text:
Files in and out of the API: uploads become artifacts, tools publish their results automatically, and both sides of the protocol reference the same opaque art_… ids.

Endpoint What it does POST /v1/files Upload one file as an artifact ({filename, media_type, data_base64}, strict JSON). GET /v1/artifacts/{id} Download the bytes (with the recorded media type). GET /v1/artifacts/{id}/meta The artifact's ArtifactRef.

docs.title: Upload, inspect, download
docs.text:
$ B64=$(base64 -w0 report.txt)
$ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:11440/v1/files -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d "{\"filename\": \"report.txt\", \"media_type\": \"text/plain\", \"data_base64\": \"$B64\"}"

{
  "id": "art_a6d3394b39b25a3c46dc1a0f3ed7b363",
  "media_type": "text/plain",
  "filename": "report.txt",
  "size": 39,
  "sha256": "ed65e35aba78802e9b12af061950641db032e9c5ab938fe01750134801816608",
  "source": "user",
  "turn_id": null,
  "session_id": null,
  "created_at": "2026-10-18T13:23:03.002384-03:00",
  "url": "/v1/artifacts/art_a6d3394b39b25a3c46dc1a0f3ed7b363"
}

GET /meta returns the same ref; GET the artifact returns the bytes:

$ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:11440/v1/artifacts/art_a6d3394b… -o report.txt
$ head -c 60 report.txt
Quarterly report draft.
Revenue is up.

A sha256 mismatch is impossible by construction — the hash and size come from the stored bytes, not the request.

docs.title: Using an artifact in a message
docs.text:
Messages reference ids with a file content part — in agent turns and in OpenAI messages alike:

{"role": "user", "content": [
  {"type": "text", "text": "Summarize this report in one sentence."},
  {"type": "file", "file_id": "art_a6d3394b39b25a3c46dc1a0f3ed7b363"}
]}

Text-ish files are inlined as a <file name="…"> block (the live run above answered "The company's quarterly report indicates a significant increase in revenue."); images go through the vision gate; other binaries are described but never faked. A missing or expired id is a structured 404 artifact_not_found before inference.

docs.title: Publication
docs.text:
Tool outputs publish automatically in serve: the file tools snapshot their result (regular files only) and scripts can call the approval-gated publish_artifact tool. Every publication emits artifact.created with the full ref between the approval decision and the tool.result, and the turn result lists the refs:

{"artifacts": [{"id": "art_2c008b58d34477b314406314cce2ec96",
  "media_type": "text/plain", "filename": "approve-demo.txt", "size": 15,
  "sha256": "a441a9bd…", "source": "tool", "turn_id": "turn_7cc9871fcf7d",
  "session_id": "20261018-131737-3773", "created_at": "…",
  "url": "/v1/artifacts/art_2c008b58d34477b314406314cce2ec96"}]}

A persist: false turn still registers and serves its artifacts — retention is TTL-only.

docs.title: Storage and retention
docs.text:
• Immutable snapshots under ~/etc/data/ollamarun/artifacts/ (config serve_artifact_root), index-driven lookup, sanitized display names, and a resolved-root containment invariant: every index/manifest path must resolve inside the store root.
  • Retention: serve_artifact_ttl (default 7 days; 0 keeps forever). The sweep also reaps stale reservations and debris at startup. Deleting a session never deletes its artifacts early.
  • Caps: serve_artifact_max_bytes (default 16 MiB — the base64-in-JSON request must fit the 32 MiB body cap), serve_artifact_quota_bytes (default 2 GiB, reserved under a lock so concurrent uploads cannot overshoot) → 507 artifact_quota_exceeded; oversize uploads are a 413.
  • The endpoints stay registered even with serve_agent: false (checked live), so the OpenAI surface can always send file parts.

docs.title: Event stream
docs.text:
GET /v1/agent/turns/{id}/events is the SSE stream for a turn. Each frame is named after its event type and carries a <turn_id>:<seq> id, so a reconnect resumes with ?after=N or Last-Event-ID.

A real capture of a completed simple turn (?after=0 replay), frames trimmed to their payloads:

$ curl -N 'http://127.0.0.1:11440/v1/agent/turns/turn_2e7a284c4149/events?after=0'
id: turn_2e7a284c4149:1
event: turn.started
data: {"id": "turn_2e7a284c4149:1", "seq": 1, "type": "turn.started", "turn_id": "turn_2e7a284c4149",
       "session_id": "20261018-131729-6386", "ts": "…",
       "data": {"model": "llama3.2:3b", "session_id": "…",
                "context": {"used": null, "total": 8192, "source": "loaded runner"}}}

id: turn_2e7a284c4149:2
event: message.delta
data: {… "data": {"channel": "content", "text": "pong"}}

id: turn_2e7a284c4149:3
event: message.completed
data: {… "data": {"round": 0, "content": "pong", "thinking": null,
                  "tool_calls": 0, "cancelled": null, "error": null}}

id: turn_2e7a284c4149:4
event: turn.completed
data: {… "data": {"content": "pong", "thinking": null, "tool_calls": 0, "rounds": 0,
                  "stats": {"total_duration": 1.658, "eval_tps": 12.27, …},
                  "context": {…}}}

Every payload shares the envelope: id, seq, type, turn_id, session_id, ts, and a data object per type.

docs.title: Event vocabulary
docs.text:
Type When Notable data turn.started Worker picked the turn up. model, session_id, context. message.delta Each streamed chunk. channel (content/thinking), text. message.completed One round finished. round, content, thinking, tool_calls count, cancelled, error. tool.call Model asked for a tool. name, args, detail, round. tool.result The tool finished (or was denied). name, ok, text, duration, and artifacts ids when files were published. approval.required A call parked for a decision. The full call + reason + suggestions + approval_id — see Approvals. approval.resolved A decision landed. action, run, note. artifact.created A file was published. The full ArtifactRef. session.fit A turn-start context fit ran. The fit result — see Context fits. turn.warning Non-fatal advice (context 80%, tool-support missing). message. turn.completed / turn.error / turn.cancelled Terminal events. content, rounds, stats, context, result shape.

A tool call and its result come before the round's message.completed for the round that requested them; an artifact.created rides between the approval decision and the tool.result that references it.

docs.title: Replay and gaps
docs.text:
• A subscription without ?after=/Last-Event-ID is live-only: nothing is replayed, so a finished turn yields an empty stream. Catching-up clients pass after=0 or read the status snapshot.
  • Last-Event-ID: <turn>:<seq> resumes exactly; ?after=N does the same.
  • If the ring has overwritten the client's position (serve_turn_event_buffer, default 10 000 events), the stream emits a stream.gap frame and the client recovers from the status snapshot.
  • Heartbeats are : ping comment lines every serve_sse_ping_interval (default 15 s) — they keep intermediaries from timing the stream out and are safe for any SSE client to ignore.

docs.title: Disconnects
docs.text: A dropped stream is an unsubscribe, not a cancellation: the turn keeps running and its results land in the session (checked live — status completed after the client vanished). With "settings": {"cancel_on_disconnect": true} the drop cancels instead (checked live — status cancelled within a couple of seconds). Explicit cancellation is POST .../cancel at any time.

docs.title: Context fits
docs.text: Context and placement over the API, at two speeds: a synchronous estimate and an asynchronous probe job.

docs.title: Estimate — POST /v1/agent/fit
docs.text:
Body: {model?, session_id?, mode: "gpu"|"cpu", cpu_percent, gpu_layers?, apply?}. No model loads; the same arithmetic the CLI's max-gpu/max-cpu use. apply: true writes the result to the session.

$ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:11440/v1/agent/fit -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"model": "qwen3:0.6b", "mode": "gpu"}'

{
  "model": "qwen3:0.6b", "mode": "gpu", "num_ctx": 22528,
  "source": "estimate", "bound": "max_gpu", "gpu_layers": null, "applied": false,
  "report": {
    "weights_bytes": 522653767, "weights_source": "/api/tags size",
    "kv_per_token": 114688, "kv_bytes_at_ctx": 2583691264,
    "free_bytes": 4220518400, "usable_bytes": 3146776576,
    "margin_bytes": 1073741824, "overhead_bytes": 0, "credited_bytes": 0,
    "total_layers": 29, "model_max": 40960, "capped_by_model": false,
    "ctx_no_margin": 31744, "calibrated": false,
    "devices": [{"total_bytes": 4096, "free_bytes": 4025}],
    "notes": ["all layers are placed on the GPU",
              "weights split: 103.0 MiB token embeddings + …"]
  },
  "object": "fit"
}

The report is the full working: weights, per-token KV, the usable budget after the margin, what was credited back from residents, the weights split and any notes. bound names which constraint chose the number (max_gpu/max_cpu); capped_by_model says the model's own maximum was the binding constraint.

When the machine cannot be read — no GPU probe, unreachable ssh — the estimate fails structurally rather than inventing a number:

{"error": {"message": "cannot read VRAM on http://100.107.146.36:11434",
 "type": "invalid_request_error", "param": null, "code": "fit_failed"}}   # 400

docs.title: Probe job — POST /v1/agent/fits
docs.text:
The same fit, verified by actually loading the model at candidate contexts (the API version of --probe). 202 with the job id and warnings:

{"id": "fit_bc6e2228c7af", "object": "fit", "status": "queued", "model": "qwen3:0.6b",
 "mode": "gpu", "probe": true, "apply": false, "warnings": [],
 "status_url": "/v1/agent/fits/fit_bc6e2228c7af",
 "cancel_url": "/v1/agent/fits/fit_bc6e2228c7af/cancel"}

GET /v1/agent/fits/{id} reports progress and then the result — the live run, condensed:

{"status": "running", "progress": {"stage": "machine", "mode": "gpu"}}
{"status": "running", "progress": {"stage": "probe", "mode": "gpu", "ctx": 22784, "attempt": 2, "max": 10}}
{"status": "running", "progress": {"stage": "probe", "mode": "gpu", "ctx": 22528, "attempt": 3, "max": 10}}
{"status": "completed", "progress": {"stage": "probe", "mode": "gpu", "ctx": 22272, "attempt": 4, "max": 10}}

"result": {
  "model": "qwen3:0.6b", "mode": "gpu", "num_ctx": 22272,
  "source": "probe", "bound": "max_gpu",
  "report": {"kv_per_token": 114688, "kv_bytes_at_ctx": 2466250752, …}
}

The estimate said 22 528, the probe measured 22 272 — that margin is the difference between arithmetic and a loaded runner. POST /v1/agent/fits/{id}/cancel stops a job (progress and status reflect it); completed jobs live until serve_fit_ttl (default 24 h). A job with a session_id holds that session: turns, edits and a second fit get 409 session_busy with active_fit_id, and the global cap (serve_max_active_fits, default 2) answers 429.

docs.title: Turn-start fits
docs.text:
A turn may ask for a fit instead of a number: "settings": {"num_ctx": "max-gpu"} (or "max-cpu" with settings.cpu_percent). The turn estimates at start — never a blocking probe, persists the fitted context and reports it as a typed session.fit event plus result.fit on the status:

"result": {"content": "pong", "fit": {"model": "qwen3:0.6b", "mode": "gpu",
 "num_ctx": 22528, "source": "estimate", "bound": "max_gpu", "report": {…}}}

A failed fit leaves the context unchanged and reports why; the turn proceeds either way.

docs.title: Gates
docs.text: serve_fit decides what exists: "probe" (default) allows both endpoints, "estimate" refuses probe jobs, "off" refuses the whole fit surface. The same switch guards turn-start fits. See Config file.

docs.title: Sessions
docs.text:
The durable record behind turns — the same JSON session store the CLI uses (see Storage).

Endpoint What it does GET/POST /v1/sessions List / create sessions. GET/PATCH/DELETE /v1/sessions/{id} Inspect, edit or trash one.

docs.title: Create
docs.text:
$ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:11440/v1/sessions \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"model": "llama3.2:3b", "title": "api demo session", "tags": ["infra", "demo"]}'

{
  "id": "20261018-132254-7414",
  "object": "session",
  "title": "api demo session",
  "model": "llama3.2:3b",
  "host": "http://127.0.0.1:11434",
  "remote": null,
  "created_at": "2026-10-18T13:22:54.823230-03:00",
  "updated_at": "2026-10-18T13:22:54.823284-03:00",
  "tags": ["infra", "demo"],
  "messages": 0,
  "turns": 0,
  "system": null,
  "artifacts": [],
  "active_turn_id": null
}

201 on create; the model must be installed and inside the allowlist.

docs.title: Edit
docs.text:
PATCH accepts title, model, system, tags, parameters, num_ctx and gpu_layers:

$ curl -s -X PATCH http://127.0.0.1:11440/v1/sessions/20261018-132254-7414 \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"title": "api demo (patched)", "num_ctx": 8192,
         "parameters": {"temperature": 0.4}}'

The parameters object is merged over the existing options (and validated like a turn's settings); num_ctx is a positive integer (refused past the model's trained maximum) and gpu_layers takes the CLI spec (N, P%, +N/-N, all, cpu, auto) — a placement change unloads the resident model exactly like /gpu-layers.

docs.title: Read
docs.text:
GET /v1/sessions/{id} returns the summary plus history, stats, parameters, tool_allow, tool_rules and tools_disabled — everything a client needs to render a resumed session. GET /v1/sessions lists the same summaries:

{"object": "list", "data": [{"id": "…", "title": "…", "model": "…", "host": "…",
 "created_at": "…", "updated_at": "…", "messages": 2, "turns": 0,
 "prompt_tokens": 0, "completion_tokens": 0, "tags": []}, …]}

docs.title: Delete
docs.text: DELETE /v1/sessions/{id} moves the session to the trash (trash-put, recoverable) and returns the summary with object: "session.deleted". Deleting a session never deletes its artifacts early — artifact retention is TTL-only.

docs.title: While a turn or fit runs
docs.text: A session with an active turn (or a running fit) refuses edits and deletes with 409 session_busy naming the active_turn_id/active_fit_id, and a second turn for the same session is refused the same way — see Turns.

docs.title: Maps to the CLI
docs.text: API CLI equivalent POST /v1/sessions A first run with --session NAME / --title. GET /v1/sessions/{id} ollamarun --show ID / --export ID. PATCH … {num_ctx} /num-ctx N. PATCH … {gpu_layers} /gpu-layers SPEC. DELETE ollamarun --delete ID.

docs.title: Turns
docs.text:
The same ollamarun serve process exposes ollamarun's own endpoints: instead of one inference call, a client submits a full agent turn — the internal tool loop, approvals and session persistence run server-side — and follows it over Server-Sent Events.

Endpoint What it does POST /v1/agent/turns Start a full agent turn (202 + the turn id and its URLs). GET /v1/agent/turns/{id} Snapshot: status, seq, result, error (404 unknown, 410 swept). GET /v1/agent/turns/{id}/events SSE turn events — see Event stream. POST /v1/agent/turns/{id}/cancel Request cancellation.

docs.title: Starting a turn
docs.text:
POST /v1/agent/turns
{
  "model": "llama3.2:3b",
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Reply with exactly: pong"}],
  "settings": {"tools": false, "system": "n/a"}
}

The response is immediate — the turn runs in a worker thread:

{
  "id": "turn_2e7a284c4149",
  "object": "turn",
  "session_id": "20261018-131729-6386",
  "status": "queued",
  "created_at": "2026-10-18T13:17:29.948845-03:00",
  "status_url": "/v1/agent/turns/turn_2e7a284c4149",
  "events_url": "/v1/agent/turns/turn_2e7a284c4149/events",
  "cancel_url": "/v1/agent/turns/turn_2e7a284c4149/cancel"
}

For an existing session (session_id) the messages are the delta; for a new one they seed the history. Turns persist by default (persist: false runs ephemeral — the results still land in-memory and artifacts still register). model is required when creating a session; continuing one may omit it.

docs.title: settings
docs.text:
Key Default Meaning tools true Run the tool loop. max_rounds 8 Tool rounds cap. approval "policy" "policy" decides via the allowlist/rules (denying the rest), "interactive" parks undecided calls — see Approvals. system null System-prompt override ("auto", text, or absent for none). parameters {} Validated Ollama options merged into the request. num_ctx — A window, or "max-gpu"/"max-cpu" to estimate at turn start (see Context fits). cpu_percent — With num_ctx: "max-cpu". gpu_layers — Placement spec; a change unloads the resident model. cancel_on_disconnect false Cancel when the events stream drops (default: keep running).

parameters validation is strict: known Ollama options get type and range checks, unknown names pass through bounded to scalars and small lists, and non-finite numbers or nested structures are refused with a 400.

docs.title: The snapshot
docs.text:
The status endpoint gives the same result with no stream:

{
  "id": "turn_2e7a284c4149",
  "object": "turn",
  "session_id": "20261018-131729-6386",
  "status": "completed",
  "seq": 4,
  "oldest_seq": 1,
  "latest_seq": 4,
  "truncated": false,
  "context": {"used": null, "total": 8192, "source": "loaded runner"},
  "error": null,
  "result": {
    "status": "completed",
    "content": "pong",
    "thinking": null,
    "tool_calls": null,
    "rounds": 0,
    "usage": {"prompt_tokens": 32, "completion_tokens": 2, "total_tokens": 34},
    "stats": {"total_duration": 1.658, "load_duration": 0.003, "prompt_tokens": 32,
              "completion_tokens": 2, "eval_tps": 12.27, "prompt_tps": 21.51, "done_reason": "stop"},
    "artifacts": [],
    "fit": null
  }
}
  • status is queued / running / waiting_approval / completed / failed / cancelled.
  • seq/oldest_seq/latest_seq/truncated describe the event ring (see Replay and gaps) — a late client can resume exactly.
  • context is the live window (used/total/source) when known.
  • result.artifacts lists published artifacts; result.fit carries a turn-start fit when one ran.
  • A failed turn keeps a stable error message; the raw crash text goes to the --debug log, not the client.

docs.title: Cancelling
docs.text:
$ curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:11440/v1/agent/turns/turn_d1b7a7128a1b/cancel
{"id": "turn_d1b7a7128a1b", "object": "turn", "cancel_requested": true, "status": "running"}

The response reflects the request; the cancel resolves asynchronously into a turn.cancelled terminal and the snapshot's status: "cancelled". A partial answer stays on the session. Cancellation aborts the in-flight generation, kills cancellable subprocess tools and resolves a parked approval as cancelled.

docs.title: Records and limits
docs.text:
• Turn records live in memory — a restart loses live turns (404 unknown, 410 for swept ones), while session history stays in the store.
  • One active turn per session: a second submission gets 409 session_busy with the active_turn_id; editing or deleting the session is refused the same way while the turn runs (or a fit holds it).
  • A global cap (serve_max_active_turns, default 4) answers 429:
{"error": {"message": "too many active turns", "type": "rate_limit_error",
 "param": null, "code": "rate_limit_error", "limit": 4}}
  • Completed turns are kept for serve_turn_event_ttl (default 24 h; 0 keeps them) so late clients can still replay.

  • serve_turn_timeout (default 0 = off) is a wall-clock cap; hitting it cancels the turn with reason timeout.

  • Event stream — following a turn.

  • Approvals — resolving parked tool calls.
  • Sessions — the durable record.

docs.title: Chat completions
docs.text:
POST /v1/chat/completions is one model turn, streaming or not. It is a translation proxy: one request becomes one /api/chat call upstream, and client tools pass through without ever being executed (that is the native agent API's job).

$ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:11440/v1/chat/completions \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"model": "llama3.2:3b",
         "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Reply with exactly: pong"}],
         "temperature": 0}'

{
  "id": "chatcmpl-192eef6fe6594a949b5a814a",
  "object": "chat.completion",
  "created": 1792340145,
  "model": "llama3.2:3b",
  "choices": [
    {
      "index": 0,
      "message": {"role": "assistant", "content": "pong"},
      "finish_reason": "stop"
    }
  ],
  "usage": {"prompt_tokens": 30, "completion_tokens": 2, "total_tokens": 32}
}

docs.title: Supported fields
docs.text:
Field Notes model Required; must be installed and inside the allowlist. messages OpenAI roles; assistant tool_calls and role: tool history convert back to the Ollama shape. temperature, top_p, stop, seed, presence_penalty, frequency_penalty Forwarded as Ollama options. max_tokens / max_completion_tokens → num_predict (either name works). response_format {"type":"json_object"} or json_schema → Ollama's format grammar (only the schema object is forwarded). reasoning_effort low/medium/high → Ollama think; thinking comes back as reasoning_content (see Streaming). tools, tool_choice Pass-through; auto, none or a specific function. required is rejected — see Tool calls. stream, stream_options.include_usage See Streaming. n 1..8, emulated sequentially — see n > 1 choices. parallel_tool_calls false truncates the returned calls to the first (the backend cannot be told). user, metadata Accepted and ignored (tracking hints). system (extension) "auto" = the built-in default prompt, text = replace it; absent = none. A client-sent system message always wins.

Everything else — unknown fields anywhere, logprobs, logit_bias, audio, non-text modalities — is a structured 400, never a silent ignore. The full matrix is in Errors.

docs.title: Python
docs.text:
The official SDK works unmodified:

from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(base_url="http://127.0.0.1:11440/v1", api_key="unused")
reply = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="llama3.2:3b",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "hello"}],
)
print(reply.choices[0].message.content)
  • Streaming — the SSE frame sequence.
  • Tool calls — pass-through semantics and parallel_tool_calls.
  • Vision — image_url and file parts.
  • Errors — every rejection and its envelope.

docs.title: Embeddings
docs.text:
POST /v1/embeddings maps to Ollama's /api/embed. The request shape is {model, input, encoding_format, dimensions, user}: input is a non-empty string or array of non-empty strings (a client's token arrays are rejected explicitly), encoding_format is "float" (default) or "base64" (the little-endian float32 packing the official SDK sends by default), and dimensions is forwarded for models that support truncated vectors.

$ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:11440/v1/embeddings \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"model": "nomic-embed-text", "input": "hello world"}'

{
  "object": "list",
  "model": "nomic-embed-text",
  "data": [{"object": "embedding", "index": 0, "embedding": [-0.0068, -0.0014, -0.1713, …]}],
  "usage": {"prompt_tokens": 4, "total_tokens": 4}
}

768 floats for that model — the same values whichever encoding you ask for:

$ curl -s … -d '{"model": "nomic-embed-text", "input": "hello world", "encoding_format": "base64"}'
# data[0].embedding is a base64 string; decoded:
decoded dims: 768 first3 [-0.0068, -0.0014, -0.1713]

docs.title: Gates and limits
docs.text:
• The model must advertise the embedding capability (model_does_not_support_embeddings otherwise; an unverifiable empty capability list passes — older servers).
  • The serve_models allowlist applies exactly as elsewhere.
  • Inputs are charged to the same resolved-input budget as chat content (count, per-input bytes, total text), with 413 input_too_large naming the limit.
  • The token counts in usage come from the backend, not a client-side estimate.

The CLI has the same route for one-shot use — ollamarun nomic-embed-text "hello world" prints a summary table, and --dimensions/--truncate map to the same fields (see Embeddings).

docs.title: Errors
docs.text: Request validation is strict: every rejection is a structured error with the OpenAI envelope, never a silent ignore. The captures below are verbatim responses.

docs.title: Unknown and unsupported fields
docs.text:
$ … -d '{"model": "llama3.2:3b", "messages": […], "bogus": 1}'
{"error": {"message": "unknown field: bogus", "type": "invalid_request_error",
 "param": "bogus", "code": "unknown_field"}}                       # HTTP 400

Unknown fields are rejected everywhere they can appear — top level, inside tools, tool_choice, response_format wrappers.

$ … -d '{…, "n": 9}'
{"error": {"message": "n is limited to 8 emulated generations", "type":
 "invalid_request_error", "param": "n", "code": "unsupported_value"}}

$ … -d '{…, "logprobs": true}'
{"error": {"message": "logprobs is not supported", "type":
 "invalid_request_error", "param": "logprobs", "code": "unsupported_parameter"}}

$ … -d '{…, "tool_choice": "required"}'
{"error": {"message": "tool_choice must be \"auto\", \"none\" or a specific function
 (the backend cannot force a call)", "type": "invalid_request_error",
 "param": "tool_choice", "code": "unsupported_value"}}

$ … -d '{…, "tools": [{…, "strict": true}]}'
{"error": {"message": "strict tool schemas are not supported (the backend does not
 enforce tool-argument schemas)", "type": "invalid_request_error",
 "param": "tools[0].function.strict", "code": "unsupported_parameter"}}

Also rejected: logit_bias, audio, non-text modalities, malformed message shapes, and non-integer n.

docs.title: Unknown models and upstream failures
docs.text:
{"error": {"message": "model 'nope:latest' not found",
 "type": "invalid_request_error", "param": "model", "code": "model_not_found"}}

model_not_found (404) is also what a model outside the allowlist answers. The server distinguishes:

Code Means model_not_found Unknown model or outside the allowlist. backend_unreachable The Ollama machine could not be reached (502). backend_error The backend failed the request (502), sanitized — raw detail goes to the --debug log. model_does_not_support_images / …embeddings Capability gates. input_too_large A resolved-input limit (413). not_found Unknown endpoint (404) — including agent routes when serve_agent: false.

docs.title: What is never in a response
docs.text:
Status codes are used properly (400/404/405/408/413/502), and responses never carry tracebacks or internal paths. Oversized bodies and stalled uploads are rejected before parsing; malformed chunked framing is a structured 400. --debug logs requests, upstream detail and tracebacks to ~/etc/logs/ollamarun.log for the operator — not the client.

The same envelope shape is used by the agent API; its typed errors (session_busy 409, rate_limit_error 429, expired turns 410) are listed on Turns.

docs.title: Models
n > 1 choices
docs.text:
n runs that many generations, 1..8, emulated sequentially — each choice is a full /api/chat call — with the usage counters summed:

$ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:11440/v1/chat/completions \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"model": "llama3.2:3b", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Name one color."}],
         "n": 2, "temperature": 0.9, "max_tokens": 8}'

{
  "choices": [
    {"index": 0, "message": {"role": "assistant", "content": "Blue."}, "finish_reason": "stop"},
    {"index": 1, "message": {"role": "assistant", "content": "Blue."}, "finish_reason": "stop"}
  ],
  "usage": {"prompt_tokens": 58, "completion_tokens": 6, "total_tokens": 64}
}

(That run happened to sample the same answer twice; the choices are independent samples.)

  • The choices carry index 0..n-1 in request order.
  • usage is the sum over the emulated choices.
  • On a stream, chunk deltas carry the per-choice index; the usage chunk reports the summed counters and closes the stream as always.
  • n outside 1..8 or a non-integer is rejected before any generation:
$ … -d '{"model": "llama3.2:3b", "messages": […], "n": 9}'
{"error": {"message": "n is limited to 8 emulated generations",
 "type": "invalid_request_error", "param": "n", "code": "unsupported_value"}}

Because each emulated choice is a full generation, a large n costs proportionally — on a local GPU that is real seconds, not a rounding error.

docs.title: Streaming
docs.text:
With "stream": true the response is OpenAI SSE: one data: line per chunk, data: [DONE] as the terminator. A real capture (trimmed):

$ curl -sN http://127.0.0.1:11440/v1/chat/completions \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"model": "llama3.2:3b",
         "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Count from 1 to 3, one number per line."}],
         "temperature": 0, "max_tokens": 24, "stream": true,
         "stream_options": {"include_usage": true}}'
data: {"id": "chatcmpl-d2183d18…", "object": "chat.completion.chunk", "created": 1792340150,
       "model": "llama3.2:3b",
       "choices": [{"index": 0, "delta": {"role": "assistant", "content": ""}, "finish_reason": null}]}

data: {"id": "chatcmpl-d2183d18…", …, "choices": [{"index": 0, "delta": {"content": "1"}, "finish_reason": null}]}
…
data: {"id": "chatcmpl-d2183d18…", …, "choices": [{"index": 0, "delta": {}, "finish_reason": "stop"}]}

data: {"id": "chatcmpl-d2183d18…", …, "choices": [],
       "usage": {"prompt_tokens": 38, "completion_tokens": 6, "total_tokens": 44}}

data: [DONE]

The order, every time:

  1. a role chunk (delta.role set, empty content),
  2. content deltas (one per chunk; for an n > 1 request the choice index varies),
  3. the finish chunk (delta empty, finish_reason set),
  4. the usage chunk — only with "stream_options": {"include_usage": true}; choices is [], exactly as OpenAI does it,
  5. data: [DONE].

docs.title: Thinking models, tool calls
docs.text:
• Reasoning models surface their thinking as the non-standard delta.reasoning_content (also on the non-streaming message), which normal clients ignore — verified live with minicpm-v4.6:1b.
  • A tool-call reply streams as one indexed array chunk on delta.tool_calls with finish_reason: "tool_calls" — see Tool calls.

docs.title: Disconnects
docs.text:
A dropped streaming client cancels its own upstream generation. Each request builds its own OllamaClient, so a client vanishing only affects its own stream, never another request's. Heartbeats and the request timeout never cut a stream that is still producing.

The native agent surface has its own typed event stream with ids and replay — see Event stream; this page is the OpenAI surface only.

docs.title: Tool calls
docs.text:
Client tools are passed to the backend and returned as standard tool_calls with finish_reason: "tool_calls". They are never executed here — this endpoint cannot trigger the agent harness, sandboxes or approvals; full agent turns live under the native /v1/agent/turns endpoint.

A real request/response (llama3.2:3b asked for the weather with one function declared):

$ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:11440/v1/chat/completions \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
      "model": "llama3.2:3b",
      "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "What is the weather in Porto Alegre? Use the tool."}],
      "tools": [{"type": "function", "function": {
        "name": "get_weather", "description": "Get the weather for a city",
        "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"city": {"type": "string"}},
                       "required": ["city"]}}}],
      "temperature": 0}'

{
  "id": "chatcmpl-2ecb878a39e04dc3aa0d3d31",
  "object": "chat.completion",
  "model": "llama3.2:3b",
  "choices": [{
    "index": 0,
    "message": {
      "role": "assistant",
      "content": null,
      "tool_calls": [{
        "id": "call_elpr4nhe",
        "type": "function",
        "function": {"name": "get_weather", "arguments": "{\"city\": \"Porto Alegre\"}"}
      }]
    },
    "finish_reason": "tool_calls"
  }],
  "usage": {"prompt_tokens": 163, "completion_tokens": 17, "total_tokens": 180}
}

Note arguments is a JSON string (OpenAI's shape), and content is null when the model only calls tools. Sending the tool results back works like any OpenAI client: append the assistant message with its tool_calls, then one {"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": …, "content": …} per call — the mapper converts the history to Ollama's shape.

docs.title: Semantics worth knowing
docs.text:
Detail Behavior tool_choice auto, none, or a specific function are forwarded. "required" is rejected (400) — the backend cannot force a call. parallel_tool_calls: false Truncates the response to the first tool call. The backend cannot be told to emit only one, so this is a filter, not steering. strict: true on a function Rejected (400): tool-argument schemas are not enforced by the backend (strict: false is a no-op). response_format schemas are enforced, via Ollama's grammar. Streaming Tool calls arrive as one indexed array chunk on delta.tool_calls, then finish_reason: "tool_calls". Aliases None here — the function names are yours; the server never maps them onto its own tool registry.

For a client that wants the harness — real execution, approvals, sessions — use POST /v1/agent/turns with "settings": {"tools": true}.

docs.title: Vision
docs.text:
image_url content parts accept data: URIs or http(s) URLs (fetched with explicit timeouts, at most 3 redirects and a 10 MiB cap — the SSRF caveat is the locked trusted-network boundary). A {"type": "file", "file_id": "art_…"} part resolves an uploaded artifact instead; text-ish files are inlined as a <file name="…"> block, images go through the same vision gate, and other binaries are described but never pretended to be processed — see Artifacts.

A real request and answer (red square, minicpm-v4.6:1b):

$ B64=$(base64 -w0 red.png)
$ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:11440/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "{
    \"model\": \"minicpm-v4.6:1b\",
    \"messages\": [{\"role\": \"user\", \"content\": [
      {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"What color fills this image? Reply with one word.\"},
      {\"type\": \"image_url\", \"image_url\": {\"url\": \"data:image/png;base64,$B64\"}}]}],
    \"max_tokens\": 256}"

{
  "choices": [{
    "index": 0,
    "message": {
      "role": "assistant",
      "content": "red",
      "reasoning_content": "Got it, let's look at the image. The image is filled with a red color. …"
    },
    "finish_reason": "stop"
  }],
  …
}

Two practical notes from that run: the model's thinking came back as reasoning_content (non-standard, ignorable), and 32 max tokens were not enough — the thinking consumed the budget and content came back empty with finish_reason: "length". Give a multimodal thinking model headroom.

docs.title: The capability gate
docs.text:
Content parts are validated against the model's capabilities, so a text-only model is refused before inference:

$ … -d '{"model": "llama3.2:3b", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": [
      {"type": "text", "text": "Color?"},
      {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": "data:image/png;base64,…"}}]}]}'
{"error": {"message": "this model does not support image input",
 "type": "invalid_request_error", "param": "messages",
 "code": "model_does_not_support_images"}}          # HTTP 400

The CLI takes images too — --image PATH / /image PATH… | clear — see [Images and vision(../../cli/images.md).

docs.title: CLI overview
docs.text:
ollamarun is the terminal harness. Every ollama run flag (ollama 0.34) is accepted and extended, so it still doubles as a drop-in replacement for the CLI it started as: run it one-shot with a prompt, or with none for the interactive REPL.

  • Agent loop, not a pipe. The model calls tools through Ollama function calling — shell, Python, files, web, your saved sessions, system stats, speech, the chemical inventory — in multi-round loops. Read-only calls run unattended; everything else asks, with numbered choices and remembered rules. See Tools.
  • Rendering that keeps up. Markdown re-renders while tokens stream, display math is laid out in 2D Unicode by a self-contained engine, thinking streams live in a collapsible panel, and a ~tok/s · ctx footer ticks with every token (--no-tps//tps switch it off). See Streaming markdown.
  • Sessions that persist. One atomic JSON per conversation plus an index under ~/etc/data/ollamarun/, with search, export (md/json/html), branch, tags and trash-put deletes. See Storage.
  • Two front ends. The prompt_toolkit inline REPL (default) or --ui tui (deprecated — see TUI): transcript pane, status bar, and an input box that stays usable while the model works.
  • Any machine on the tailnet. --remote NAME runs all inference and model management on another machine — a name defined in config remote_hosts, or any host[:port] — while sessions, files and tools stay local. See Remote inference.
  • Context and placement fitting. /num-ctx --max-gpu finds the largest window that stays fully on the GPU, /num-ctx --max-cpu N fills DRAM to N%, --probe verifies by loading and calibrates later estimates, and /gpu-layers pins layer counts. See Context and placement.
  • Model-facing text is data. Tool definitions and prompts live as JSON/Markdown under ollamarun_lib/defs/, overridable per user without touching Python. See Tool definitions and Prompts.

Start with Usage and flags, or jump straight to The REPL.

docs.title: Slash commands
docs.text: Everything interactive is a slash command, dispatched identically in the inline REPL and the TUI. /help prints the live table; /help shortcuts lists the keys. Syntax below is the canonical form — prefixes and convenience spellings are noted per command.

docs.title: /model, /models [NAME | --list | --sort KEY]
docs.text:
Without an argument: the interactive picker. With a name: switch model (unloading the current one). --list prints the table instead, --sort KEY orders it (modified, name, size, parameters, context).

llama3.2:3b › /model --list --sort size

docs.title: /load [MODEL | SESSION]
docs.text:
/load SESSION resumes a saved session; if its model differs from the current one, it asks current or last and unloads on the switch. /load MODEL is a model switch (/model with a different verb):

llama3.2:3b › /load llama3.2:3b
already using that model

See Save and load.

docs.title: /save NAME
docs.text:
Creates an Ollama model from the session — messages plus the effective system prompt:

llama3.2:3b › /save olladocs-test:latest
creating olladocs-test:latest from llama3.2:3b…
  … writing manifest
  success
created olladocs-test:latest — `ollamarun olladocs-test:latest`

docs.title: /clear, /new [TITLE]
docs.text:
/clear empties the context but keeps settings (a fresh session id under the same file); /new saves the current session and starts a brand-new one.

llama3.2:3b › /clear
context cleared
llama3.2:3b › /new fresh start
new session 20261018-122626-02cd

docs.title: /sessions [filter]
docs.text: The session browser: a numbered table, then session number, ID, filter or 'q' to quit. Typing text filters; a number or id switches. See Search and export.

docs.title: /bye, /exit
docs.text:
Save and leave (Ctrl+D does the same). Unloads the session model unless --keep-loaded/housekeeping.

llama3.2:3b › /bye
unloaded llama3.2:3b
session 20261018-124236-e402 saved · ~/etc/data/ollamarun/sessions

docs.title: /title [TEXT | --auto]
docs.text: Show, set, or ask the model to (re)title the session — see Titles and tags.

docs.title: /tag [list | add TAG… | rm TAG]
docs.text:
Session tags: add/rm take several at once.

llama3.2:3b › /tag add demo docs
tags demo, docs

docs.title: /branch [TITLE]
docs.text:
Fork the conversation into a new session (settings, rules and tags included) and switch to it — see Branching.

llama3.2:3b › /branch side quest
branched 20261018-122252-de60

docs.title: /undo, /retry, /edit
docs.text:
llama3.2:3b › /undo
undone
llama3.2:3b › /retry
retrying…
llama3.2:3b › /edit
resending edited message…

/undo drops the last exchange as a unit; /retry keeps the question and regenerates; /edit reopens the last user message in $OLLAMA_EDITOR and resends the edited text. Full semantics in Undo, retry and edit and Editor.

docs.title: /copy [N]
docs.text: Copies the last response (or its Nth code block) to the clipboard. Needs pyperclip; reports pyperclip is not installed otherwise.

docs.title: /set parameter NAME [VALUE], /set system TEXT
docs.text:
Set a model option (values are coerced: 0.2 → float, true → bool, JSON passes through); no value clears it. /set system is the system prompt.

llama3.2:3b › /set parameter temperature 0.2
set temperature = 0.2

docs.title: /params
docs.text: The session's parameters table — see Parameters.

docs.title: /think [on | off | low | medium | high]
docs.text:
The model's thinking mode (sent as Ollama's think). /thinking controls the display instead — see Thinking panel.

llama3.2:3b › /think low
think low

docs.title: /show [info | license | modelfile | parameters | system | template]

Model details, ollama show-style. info prints the model table and the session parameters together:

docs.title: /pull [MODEL]
docs.text:
Pull or update a model on the Ollama machine with live progress — see Pulling models.

llama3.2:3b › /pull llama3.2:3b
llama3.2:3b is installed — checking for updates
pulling llama3.2:3b · pulling manifest …

docs.title: /ps
docs.text:
Resident models (ollama ps) with VRAM, quant and keep-alive countdown.

llama3.2:3b › /ps
                                ollama ps
│ model       │ size    │ VRAM    │ quant  │ until               │
│ llama3.2:3b │ 3.2 GiB │ 2.7 GiB │ Q4_K_M │ 2026-10-18 12:51:04 │

docs.title: /num-ctx [N | --max-gpu [--probe] | --max-cpu N [--probe]]
docs.text:
The window size, the GPU fit or the DRAM fill — num-ctx and the context overview.

qwen3:0.6b › /num-ctx 8192
num_ctx set to 8192
qwen3:0.6b › /num-ctx 99999999
99999999 exceeds qwen3:0.6b's max context (40960) — capped to 40960

With no argument it prints the current value, the model's maximum and the two fit forms.

docs.title: /gpu-layers [N | N% | +N | -N | all | cpu | auto]
docs.text:
Pin the GPU/CPU layer split — GPU layers.

qwen3:0.6b › /gpu-layers 50%
gpu layers 50% → 15 of 29 layers
unloaded qwen3:0.6b
the model will reload with the new setting

docs.title: /context
docs.text:
Window usage: message counts, last request's tokens, effective length.

llama3.2:3b › /context
│ messages               │     2 │
│ last prompt tokens     │    94 │
│ context used           │   100 │
│ context length         │  8192 │

docs.title: /summarize
docs.text: Compact the older half of the conversation into a summary — Compaction.

docs.title: /tools [SPEC]
docs.text:
The whole harness lives here:

Form Effect /tools (or list/status) The state table and the policy line. /tools on \| off Enable/disable the harness for the session. /tools policy auto\|allowlist\|ask Global approval policy. /tools enable NAME… \| disable NAME… Toggle several tools. /tools NAME on \| off Toggle one tool (aliases resolve). /tools NAME help Generated from the definition JSON. /tools NAME call ARGS Run it yourself through the approval gate. /tools allow The safe shell-command allowlist. /tools rules [add\|rm] Stored approval rules. /tools help The reference table.

See Tools and Approvals and policy.

docs.title: /render [markdown | plain | raw]
docs.text:
Response rendering — Streaming markdown.

llama3.2:3b › /render plain
render plain

docs.title: /math [on | off]
docs.text:
LaTeX → Unicode conversion — 2D math.

llama3.2:3b › /math off
math off

docs.title: /thinking [show | collapse | hide | toggle | full]
docs.text: Thinking display; full prints the stored reasoning after the fact — Thinking panel.

docs.title: /tps [on | off]
docs.text:
The live tokens/s + context footer — Footer.

llama3.2:3b › /tps off
tps footer off

docs.title: /pager [on | off]
docs.text: Buffer responses into $PAGER — Pager.

docs.title: /image PATH… | clear
docs.text: Attach images to the next message; clear drops pending ones — Images and vision.

docs.title: /export [--format md|json|html] [FILE]
docs.text:
Export the current session, mid-run — same formats as the CLI --export:

llama3.2:3b › /export --format md /tmp/session.md
wrote /tmp/session.md

docs.title: /queue [list | clear | rm N]
docs.text:
What is waiting while a turn runs — the queue is the deprecated TUI's typing-ahead list; the inline REPL reads one line at a time.

llama3.2:3b › /queue list
queue is empty

docs.text: Auto-speak final answers through tts-remote; tools toggles the model's speech tools — see Tools and the config keys tts_*.

docs.title: Editor
docs.text: Two ways to bring a real editor into a conversation.

docs.title: Ctrl+G: edit the current input
docs.text:
Press Ctrl+G at the prompt and the current input opens in $OLLAMA_EDITOR — or $EDITOR when OLLAMA_EDITOR is unset, falling back to vi. The buffer is written to a temporary .md file, the editor is launched on it, and whatever you save replaces the input line when the editor exits:

$ OLLAMA_EDITOR=nano ollamarun --no-tools llama3.2:3b
llama3.2:3b › a half-written question        ← press Ctrl+G here

In the editor you fix the text, save and quit, and the prompt comes back with the new content — then Enter sends it. Tested end-to-end with a scripted editor that replaced draft text with a question: the answer that came back was for the edited prompt.

  • An editor that cannot be started prints editor failed: … and the input is left untouched.
  • OLLAMA_EDITOR is split shell-style, so OLLAMA_EDITOR="code --wait" or any command with arguments works.
  • For quick aliases, export it once in your shell profile.

docs.title: /edit: redo the last message
docs.text:
/edit reopens the last user message in the same editor and resends it: the edited text replaces the old message, everything after it is dropped and the model answers again. It is the undo/retry family's scalpel — /retry resends unchanged, /undo just drops.

Tested flow:

llama3.2:3b › Name one color. Answer with one word.
Blue
llama3.2:3b › /edit
resending edited message…
Apple

The editor was prefilled with the original message and returned Name one fruit. Answer with one word.; the old exchange was replaced, not appended. An empty result cancels (edit cancelled) and nothing is sent.

docs.title: Front ends
docs.text: The inline REPL binds Ctrl+G to the current input. In the deprecated Textual TUI the same key opens $EDITOR; /edit works in both.

docs.title: @file mentions
docs.text: @path in a prompt inlines the file's contents into the message: the model sees the text itself, not the path. It works in the REPL, in one-shot prompts and for piped stdin alike, and is the quick way to hand a file to a model without a tool call.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
• @ immediately before a path; the path runs to the next whitespace.
  • ~ expands to your home; relative paths resolve against the working directory the harness runs in.
  • Several mentions in one prompt are all inlined.
  • In the REPL, Tab completes @files along with commands, ids and model names.

The contents are appended to the message as one block per file, so the model can tell where a file starts and ends:

<file name="/tmp/notes.txt">
The fjord holds a copper coin of moon.
Second line, unremarkable.
</file>

The path is part of the block header; the user message itself keeps the mention as typed, and the session records the resolved paths so /show and exports can list what was sent.

docs.title: Tested examples
docs.text:
With this file:

$ printf 'The fjord holds a copper coin of moon.\nSecond line, unremarkable.\n' > /tmp/notes.txt

Ask about it — note the space before the ?, which is what ends the path:

$ ollamarun --no-tools --no-save llama3.2:3b "What is the first line of @/tmp/notes.txt ? Reply with just that line, verbatim."
llama3.2:3b ›
The fjord holds a copper coin of moon.

A missing file and an over-limit file both warn and are skipped (the model simply does not get them):

$ ollamarun --no-tools --no-save llama3.2:3b "Summarize @/tmp/nope.txt in one word."
@/tmp/nope.txt: no such file
llama3.2:3b ›
I don't see any file at `/tmp/nope.txt`.

$ ollamarun --no-tools --no-save llama3.2:3b "Summarize @/tmp/big.txt in one word."
@/tmp/big.txt: 300 KiB exceeds 256 KiB limit

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
Setting Default Meaning max_file_kb (config) 256 Files larger than this are skipped with a warning. — — Files are read as UTF-8 with undecodable bytes replaced.

Because the content is appended to the prompt, a big file eats the context window — the context counter and /context show the damage, and compaction can trim older messages.

Punctuation ends the mention

The path ends only at whitespace, so a sentence-final ./,/) right after the mention becomes part of the filename and the file is not inlined:

$ ollamarun --no-tools --no-save llama3.2:3b "Summarize @/tmp/notes.txt. One word."
@/tmp/notes.txt.: no such file

Put a space between the path and the punctuation (@/tmp/notes.txt .) or reorder the sentence. Tracked as issue #39.

docs.title: Where it fits
docs.text:
• Images and vision attaches images the same way, but as vision input instead of text.
  • The file tools (read_file, write_file, …) let the model decide what to touch; @file is you deciding up front.

docs.title: Images and vision
docs.text: Images ride along with a message as vision input. They are attached to the next message only — once it is sent, the attachment is spent, and /image clear throws pending ones away.

docs.title: Attaching
docs.text:
Way When --image PATH (repeatable) At launch, for a one-shot or the REPL's first message. /image PATH… In the REPL, for the next message. /image clear Drop everything pending.

The command answers with what it queued:

minicpm-v4.6:1b › /image /tmp/red.png
attached red.png
minicpm-v4.6:1b › What color fills the attached image? Answer with one word.
red

The model must advertise vision. Asking a text-only model makes the backend refuse the request, and the harness surfaces that as an ordinary error:

$ ollamarun --no-tools --no-save --image /tmp/red.png llama3.2:3b "What color is this image?"
llama3.2:3b ›
HTTP 400 on /api/chat: Multimodal data provided, but model does not support
multimodal requests.

A missing file exits 2 with the path as the message — currently without further context (tracked as issue #40):

$ ollamarun --no-save --image /tmp/does-not-exist.png llama3.2:3b "hi"
/tmp/does-not-exist.png
$ echo $?
2

docs.title: How they are sent
docs.text:
Images are base64-embedded into the chat request (images on the Ollama message), so nothing about the target machine matters: with --remote the file stays local and travels with the request.

  • Config image_storage (default "embed") keeps the bytes in the pending record. With any other value, files over 8 MiB are kept as a path and re-read when the request is built instead of being embedded twice.
  • Everything is read from disk at attach time, so editing the file afterwards does not change what was sent (in embed mode).

docs.title: The API side
docs.text: ollamarun serve takes images as OpenAI image_url parts (data URIs or http(s) URLs) or as uploaded file parts, with its own capability check and limits — see Vision and Artifacts.

docs.title: Pager
docs.text:
--pager (config pager: true) buffers the response and opens it in the system pager when it is complete, instead of streaming it into the scrollback:

$ PAGER=cat ollamarun --no-tools --pager llama3.2:3b "Reply with a two-item markdown bullet list of primary colors."
 • Red
 • Blue

The pager is the standard one: rich hands the content to pydoc's pager, which uses $PAGER (commonly less; PAGER=cat above prints it straight through, which is also what happens when the output is piped). Inside the pager you scroll and search the way that tool works; quitting it returns to the prompt.

/pager [on|off] toggles it mid-session:

llama3.2:3b › /pager on
pager: on

What lands in the pager is the finished answer with the same rendering — including the thinking panel when it is visible, and the response divider when a tool loop preceded it. What you lose is the live view: while the model generates, the terminal stays quiet and the footer does not tick. For long answers in a short terminal that trade is worth it; for watching progress it is not.

  • Streaming markdown — the live path.
  • Transcript replay — scrolling a session after the fact instead of during.

docs.title: Remote inference
docs.text:
--remote NAME retargets every Ollama call at another machine on your tailnet: inference, model management (/api/ps, load/unload) and /pull happen there, while sessions, files, images and the tool harness stay local. There is no separate remote code path — the same client, the same commands, a different base URL.

$ ollamarun --remote kiddo --no-tools llama3.2:3b "Reply with exactly: pong"
llama3.2:3b ›
pong

docs.title: Names and resolution
docs.text:
Short name Tailscale node pi vinipi kiddo kiddo g3 g3 optiplex7070, optiplex optiplex7070 guri guri

Anything else is treated as a hostname or host[:port], and remote_hosts in the config maps your own names to machines. Resolution reads tailscale status --json and uses the peer's tailnet IP (falling back to the MagicDNS name), so --remote tower works for any node — not only the short list above. remote_ssh_user in the config names a non-default ssh user for the probes below.

docs.title: The preflight
docs.text:
Before starting, the harness probes /api/version with a short (4 s) timeout and fails fast with what it knows:

$ ollamarun --remote tower --no-save llama3.2:3b "hi"
cannot reach remote tower at http://100.105.136.73:11434:
HTTPConnectionPool(host='100.105.136.73', port=11434): Max retries exceeded
with url: /api/version …
$ echo $?
1

The same failure happens on a live node with the wrong port (--remote kiddo:9) in about a second. For the known short names, when tailscale itself reports the node offline, the message appends the state — — tailscale reports kiddo offline — so a powered-off machine is not confused with a down Ollama.

docs.title: Probes on the remote machine
docs.text:
When something needs a machine fact — free disk before a pull, free VRAM for a context fit, available DRAM for max-cpu — a --remote session gets it over one BatchMode ssh probe (reading OLLAMA_MODELS from the ollama unit for the disk path). The system_status tool reads the same numbers, and target="local" flips to the machine you are sitting at:

llama3.2:3b › /tools system_status call
│ kiddo (ollama at http://100.107.146.36:11434)          │
│ RAM: 7.8 GiB free of 11.4 GiB                          │
│ GPU: no nvidia-smi data                                │
│ disk (models): 784.3 GiB free of 915.3 GiB at /        │

llama3.2:3b › /tools system_status call target=local
│ this machine                                           │
│ RAM: 16.9 GiB free of 31.2 GiB                         │
│ GPU 0: 729.0 MiB free of 4.0 GiB                       │
│ disk (models): 92.9 GiB free of 467.3 GiB at /usr/share/ollama/.ollama/models │

A probe that cannot reach the machine degrades to unknown rather than failing the command that needed it.

docs.title: Sticky sessions
docs.text:
Sessions store the machine they last ran on, and resuming reconnects there:

$ ollamarun --remote kiddo --no-tools --session remote-demo llama3.2:3b \
    "Remember the word: anchor. Reply OK."
OK
$ ollamarun --no-tools -c remote-demo "What word did I ask you to remember?"
resuming session on kiddo (http://100.107.146.36:11434)
The word "anchor"

Passing --host/--remote on the resume overrides the stored target.

docs.title: What stays local
docs.text: Everything that is not inference: sessions (one store, wherever you run from), @file inlining, images (sent with the request), the tool harness and its results, exports. ollamarun serve --remote NAME applies to the API layer the same way — the listener is still local, the upstream is the remote.

docs.title: The REPL
docs.text: With no PROMPT argument, ollamarun starts the interactive front end: the inline prompt_toolkit REPL (the default, --ui inline). A model-less run opens the picker first.

docs.title: Starting up
docs.text:
$ ollamarun llama3.2:3b

The banner names what is in effect:

╭─ ollamarun ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ model   llama3.2:3b                                                  │
│ session 20261018-105614-b08e · new session                           │
│ host    http://127.0.0.1:11434                                       │
│ render  markdown · thinking collapsed · 95 local models              │
│ /help for commands · Ctrl+D to exit · Ctrl+T thinking                │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
llama3.2:3b ›

The model starts loading in the background the moment the session opens — the prompt is available immediately, with a waiting for <model>… spinner on its right while the load runs. When the model becomes resident, a one-time ollama ps table prints what is loaded and for how long.

docs.title: Typing prompts
docs.text:
• Plain text goes to the model and streams back with the live footer and, for thinking models, the collapsed thinking panel.
  • @path inlines a file's contents — see @file mentions.
  • /command runs a slash command — the full set is in Slash commands.
  • Tab completes commands, session ids, model names and @files.
  • Up/Down walks the prompt history (kept in ~/etc/data/ollamarun/history; set OLLAMA_NOHISTORY to disable it).
  • Ctrl+J inserts a newline for multi-line prompts.
  • Ctrl+R searches the prompt history.
  • Ctrl+G opens $OLLAMA_EDITOR on the current input — see Editor.
  • Ctrl+D leaves (equivalent to /bye).

docs.title: While an answer streams
docs.text:
The input line becomes a rule above the live view; keystrokes are not read until the turn ends. Two keys work mid-stream:

  • Ctrl+T expands the thinking panel in place; press it again to collapse. The stream never pauses either way.
  • Ctrl+C cancels: generation stops, providers that support abort are told to stop, and the prompt returns with a cancelled note.
llama3.2:3b › ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
cancelled
llama3.2:3b ›

(The queueing behavior — typing ahead while the model works and having the message land at the next sub-task boundary — belongs to the deprecated Textual TUI; the inline REPL reads one line at a time.)
