docs.title: Leaving
docs.text:
/bye (or /exit, or Ctrl+D) ends the session. The session is saved on the way out, and — unless --keep-loaded / config unload_on_exit: false — the model is unloaded:

llama3.2:3b › /bye
session 20261018-105614-b08e saved · ~/etc/data/ollamarun/sessions

Sessions are persistent: -c continues the most recent one and --session NAME continues a named one.

Without prompt_toolkit

prompt_toolkit powers the input line. If the package is missing (or the output is not a terminal), the REPL still runs, but with plain input() prompts: no Tab completion, no history, no Ctrl+G/Ctrl+R. Install it as shown in Installation to get the real thing.

docs.title: The other front end
docs.text: --ui tui starts the Textual TUI — panes, an always-available input box and a message queue. It is deprecated ahead of the web-UI rewrite; the inline REPL is the supported front end.

docs.title: Usage and flags
docs.text:
Every ollama run flag (ollama 0.34) is accepted, and the harness adds its own on top. Three invocation shapes:

$ ollamarun [flags] MODEL [PROMPT]      # flags first
$ ollamarun MODEL [PROMPT] [flags]      # or after the prompt
$ ollamarun                             # no model: picker, then the REPL

With a prompt the run is one generation and exits; without one it is the interactive REPL (a piped stdin counts as the prompt too).

Keep flags out of the middle

A flag between MODEL and PROMPT — ollamarun llama3.2:3b --no-tools "hi" — is an argument-parsing error (unrecognized arguments: hi). Put the flags before the model or after the prompt, as above. (Tracked as issue #37.)

The reference below is the same surface as ollamarun --help, grouped by what the flags are for.

docs.title: Model and server
docs.text: Flag Default Meaning MODEL (positional) — Model name; omit it to open the picker. -m MODEL, --model MODEL — Same as the positional, for scripts that build arguments up. --host HOST[:PORT] OLLAMA_HOST or the host config key, then 127.0.0.1:11434 The Ollama server to talk to. --remote NAME — Run on a tailnet machine (pi, kiddo, g3, optiplex7070/optiplex, guri, or any host[:port]). See Remote inference. --pull off Pull the model when it is missing without asking (free-disk line and per-layer progress). See Pulling models. --sort KEY modified Order for the model picker and lists: modified, name, size, parameters, context (aliases like recent/newest work). See Picker and sorting. --insecure off Skip TLS verification for an HTTPS host (the same escape hatch ollama has).

docs.title: Prompt input
docs.text:
Flag Default Meaning --system TEXT built-in default Replace the system prompt for this run. See Prompts. --system-file FILE — Read the replacement from a file. --no-system — Send no system prompt at all. --option KEY=VALUE — A model option (-o temperature=0.7); repeatable. --options-json JSON — Model options as one JSON object. --image PATH — Attach an image for a vision model; repeatable. See Images and vision.

@path mentions inside the prompt inline files — see @file mentions.

docs.title: Context and placement
docs.text:
Flag Default Meaning --num-ctx [N\|max-gpu] model/server default Set the context window, or ask for the largest one that stays fully on the GPU. Capped to the model's trained maximum with a warning. --max-cpu N — With --num-ctx: raise the window until the model's host RAM fills N% (1-100) of the available DRAM. --probe off With --num-ctx max-gpu/--max-cpu: verify by loading the model and reading the split back from /api/ps. --gpu-layers SPEC auto N layers, P% of them, +N/-N adjustments, all, cpu or auto.

All of this (and how the fits are computed) lives in Context and placement.

docs.title: Output and rendering
docs.text: Flag Default Meaning --render {auto,markdown,plain,raw} auto auto = markdown on a terminal, plain when piped (an explicit markdown degrades to plain off-terminal too). --no-math off Disable LaTeX → Unicode conversion. See 2D math. --show-thinking collapsed Start with the thinking panel expanded. --hidethinking — Hide the thinking output. --no-tps off Hide the live tok/s + context footer. --nowordwrap off Don't wrap long lines to the terminal width. --pager off Buffer the answer into $PAGER (rich's pager) instead of streaming it in place. See Pager. --raw — Write only the answer text to stdout (no panels, no stats). --json — With a chat run: print the final Ollama response as JSON (model, message with thinking, usage, timings). With --list/--search: JSON output. --verbose off Obsolete for a terminal (timings always show there); adds the ⏱ timings line to piped/redirected output.

docs.title: Tools and speech
docs.text: Flag Default Meaning --tools on (config tools) Offer the built-in tool definitions to the model. --no-tools — Disable the tool harness for this run. -y, --yes off Auto-approve tool runs (and --delete). Use with care — see Approvals and policy. --speak config tts_auto Read every final answer aloud through tts-remote (fire-and-forget). --no-speak — Never auto-speak for this run.

docs.title: Sessions
docs.text:
Flag Default Meaning -c [SESSION_ID], --continue [SESSION_ID] — Continue the latest session, or the given one. -r, --resume — Browse saved sessions and pick one. --session NAME — Continue the session saved under NAME, or create it. --new — Force a fresh session even with -c/--session. --title TEXT — Title for a new session. --tag TAG — Tag for the session; repeatable. --auto-title config auto_title Ask the model for a title after the first turn. --no-save off Keep this run out of the session store entirely.

Sessions and their files are covered in Sessions.

docs.title: Session inspection
docs.text:
These all share one output convention — a rich table on a terminal, or --json / --csv / --markdown with --out FILE for scripts:

Flag Meaning --list List saved sessions. --search TEXT Search messages across saved sessions. --show SESSION_ID Replay a saved transcript the way it looked live. --export SESSION_ID Export a session. --export-format {md,json,html} Export format (default md). --delete SESSION_ID Move a session to the trash (trash-put; asks first unless -y). --reindex Rebuild the session index from the session files. --out FILE Write the inspection output to a file instead of stdout.

See Search and export.

docs.title: Runtime and housekeeping
docs.text: Flag Default Meaning --timeout SECONDS 600 Per-request timeout. --keepalive DURATION config keepalive How long Ollama keeps the model loaded (5m, 2h, …). --think [STR] config think Thinking mode: true/false or high/medium/low for supported models. --unload off Unload the model when the program ends (one-shot included). --keep-loaded — Never unload on exit (overrides config unload_on_exit). --ui MODE inline inline, tui (deprecated) or auto. See TUI. --config FILE ~/etc/config_files/ollamarun.json Use a different config file. --debug off Log to ~/etc/logs/ollamarun.log. --version — Print the version and exit.

docs.title: Ollama-compatible pass-through
docs.text:
Accepted for parity with ollama run and mapped onto the harness: --think, --keepalive, --hidethinking, --nowordwrap, --verbose (see above), plus:

Flag Meaning --dimensions int Truncate output embeddings to this dimension (embedding models). --truncate [bool] For embedding models: truncate inputs over the context window (default true; --truncate=false errors instead). --format string Response format — json, or an inline JSON schema (Ollama's format). With a format set, the tool harness steps aside. --insecure Skip TLS verification (HTTPS hosts).

docs.title: Environment
docs.text: Variable Meaning OLLAMA_HOST Server address when neither --host nor --remote is given. OLLAMA_EDITOR Editor for Ctrl+G and /edit (falls back to $EDITOR, then vi). See Editor. OLLAMA_NOHISTORY Do not keep the prompt input history.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text: Code When 0 Success — including a declined delete (kept) and a one-shot whose answer arrived. 1 Runtime failures: unknown session, connection/HTTP errors, a run that could not complete. 2 Usage and configuration errors: bad arguments, an invalid serve_* key, an unusable --config. 130 The run was cancelled (Ctrl+C).

docs.title: Compaction
docs.text: Long conversations eventually press against the context window. Compaction replaces the older half of the history with a summary the model wrote, so the thread continues without the raw transcript.

docs.title: The warning
docs.text:
At 80% of the effective window, the REPL says exactly what to do:

context 13112/16384 tokens (80%) — /summarize to compact

It is printed once per turn boundary (the same context_warning() call means the agent API emits a turn.warning event at the start of a turn instead of printing).

docs.title: /summarize
docs.text:
llama3.2:3b › /summarize
summarize 2 older messages? [y/n] (y): y
summarizing…
compacted 2 messages → summary

What happens, in order:

  1. Messages older than the tail are gathered. The tail that is kept is the last 2 messages when the count is even, otherwise the last 1 — so the split never cuts an exchange in half.
  2. You confirm (Y by default). Fewer than four messages is a no-op (not enough messages to summarize).
  3. A one-shot, non-streaming request is sent with the summarize.md prompt wrapping the transcript.
  4. On success the history becomes:
user       [Summary of earlier conversation]
           <the model's summary>
assistant  Understood — continuing from that summary.
<the kept tail>

An empty summary is refused (empty summary; keeping messages) and nothing changes. 5. The session is saved, and the last-prompt/completion counters reset to unknown until the next request measures again.

The replacement is written to the session file, so it is not undone by /undo — the old messages are gone once it lands.

docs.title: Automatic compaction
docs.text:
Config auto_compact picks the policy:

Value Behavior "ask" (default) Only the 80% warning; compaction stays in your hands. "auto" At 85% with more than four messages the REPL prints context almost full — summarizing older messages and summarizes without asking.

The agent API runs the "auto" path headlessly at turn start regardless of the front end's configuration — a turn that would overflow compacts first and reports the warning on its event stream.

Compaction is a model call like any other: it costs one round trip (with think disabled) and produces a user/assistant pair that the next request carries. If the summary quality matters to your workflow, keep "ask" and edit the transcript yourself before saying yes.

docs.title: GPU layers
docs.text: /gpu-layers pins how many of the model's layers run on the GPU; the rest go to the CPU. It is stored on the session, re-resolved per model, and wins over a raw num_gpu option.

docs.title: The spec
docs.text:
Spec Meaning N An absolute count. P% A percentage of the model's layers — block_count from /api/show (29 for qwen3:0.6b below). +N / -N Adjust the current value (baseline: the session's current spec, else a full offload). all Every layer on the GPU. cpu No layers on the GPU. auto Back to Ollama's own decision. 
qwen3:0.6b › /gpu-layers 50%
gpu layers 50% → 15 of 29 layers
unloaded qwen3:0.6b
the model will reload with the new setting
qwen3:0.6b › /gpu-layers
gpu layers 50% → 15 of 29 layers
N (absolute), P% (of the model's layers), +N/-N (adjust the current value), all, cpu or auto
qwen3:0.6b › /gpu-layers auto
gpu layers auto (ollama decides)

Three things worth noting in that transcript:

  • The percentage resolves against this model's layer count (29) at command time, so switching models later re-resolves the spec for the new model instead of reusing a stale number.
  • Changing the placement unloads a resident model — num_gpu is a load-time property, so the next request reloads with the new split. The command says so rather than silently keeping the old runner.
  • /gpu-layers with no argument shows the current value plus the accepted forms.

docs.title: Where it is used
docs.text:
• Launch flag: --gpu-layers SPEC; config key gpu_layers seeds it.
  • Session field: it persists across --load/-c, and the context fits honor it — when a placement is pinned, the output layer and the topmost blocks are counted as offloaded, not the whole model.
  • API: PATCH /v1/sessions/{id} and turn settings accept gpu_layers with the same spec and the same unload behavior — see Sessions API.
  • /params reports it as gpu layers (resolved label or auto (ollama decides)).

A pinned spec beats /set parameter num_gpu in the payload: the session setting is the managed path, and the resolved number is what actually goes into the request's options.

docs.title: max-cpu
docs.text:
/num-ctx --max-cpu N is the other direction: instead of keeping the model on the GPU, it raises the context window until the model's host RAM fills N% (1-100) of the DRAM available to it. The GPU keeps whatever layers the budget allows; the rest runs on the CPU.

llama3.2:3b › /num-ctx --max-cpu 80
          context fit · llama3.2:3b on this machine
╭────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ model          │ 3.21B params · Q4_K_M · llama · 1.9 GiB   │
│ machine memory │ 31.2 GiB total · 16.0 GiB available       │
│ model now      │ 6.8 GiB of host RAM (back on reload)      │
│ budget         │ 22.8 GiB = available + the resident model │
│ target         │ 18.2 GiB = 80% of the budget              │
│ placement      │ gpu-layers ~1 of 29 (fitted)              │
│ cpu weights    │ 1.7 GiB of 1.9 GiB                        │
│ kv cache       │ 112.0 KiB per token · 14.0 GiB at 131,072 │
│ overhead       │ 256.0 MiB reserved                        │
│ model max      │ 131,072 tokens                            │
╰────────────────┴───────────────────────────────────────────╯
· the loaded model holds 6.8 GiB of host RAM -- counted back into the budget, a reload returns it
· calibrated from 1 measured context point(s): 112.0 KiB per token
· weights split: 236.2 MiB token embeddings + 236.2 MiB output layer (separate) + 1.4 GiB blocks
num_ctx 131,072 (capped by the model's max context)
· at the model's max the host holds 15.9 GiB = 69% of the budget (80% requested)
estimate only — /num-ctx --max-cpu --probe loads the model and verifies the real host RAM
num_ctx set to 131072

Reading that report:

  • budget = MemAvailable (/proc/meminfo on the Ollama machine, one ssh probe for --remote) plus the RAM the loaded model already holds — a reload returns it.
  • target = N% of the budget. If the target sits beyond the model's maximum context, the cap binds and the note at the bottom says by how much (69% of the budget (80% requested)).
  • cpu weights = the share of the weights that will live in host RAM, given the placement the fit chose.
  • kv cache = per-token KV (the same profile max-gpu uses) times the candidate context.
  • overhead = max_cpu_overhead_mb (default 256 MiB) reserved for everything that is not weights or KV.

A pinned /gpu-layers is honored: with cpu every layer counts on the host side; with a fixed N, only the host share does. Without a pin the fit itself decides how many layers stay on the GPU (the gpu-layers ~1 of 29 (fitted) line above) before sizing the CPU side.

docs.title: Config and verification
docs.text:
Knob Default Meaning max_cpu_overhead_mb 256 Host-RAM allowance beyond weights + KV. max_cpu_probes 10 Load attempts a --probe may spend.

CLI: --num-ctx --max-cpu N (with --probe to verify by loading — see Probes and calibration). Like the GPU fit, this is an estimate: it is meant to pick a sensible starting window, and the probe exists for when close counts.

docs.title: max-gpu
docs.text:
/num-ctx --max-gpu answers one question: what is the largest context window that still keeps every layer of this model on the GPU? It profiles the model, measures the machine, does the arithmetic, and writes the result to the session.

llama3.2:3b › /num-ctx --max-gpu
        context fit · llama3.2:3b on this machine
╭────────────┬───────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ model      │ 3.21B params · Q4_K_M · llama · 1.9 GiB   │
│ gpu memory │ 3.9 GiB free                              │
│ margin     │ 1.0 GiB per device → 2.9 GiB usable       │
│ weights    │ 1.9 GiB                                   │
│ kv cache   │ 112.0 KiB per token · 1008.0 MiB at 9,216 │
│ model max  │ 131,072 tokens                            │
╰────────────┴───────────────────────────────────────────╯
· all layers are placed on the GPU
· weights split: 236.2 MiB token embeddings + 236.2 MiB output layer (separate) + 1.4 GiB blocks
num_ctx 9,216
estimate only — /num-ctx --max-gpu --probe loads the model and verifies the real GPU split
num_ctx set to 9216

That run is from a 4 GB GTX 1050 with a 1.9 GiB Q4 model: 2.9 GiB usable after llama.cpp's fit margin, 1.9 GiB of weights, 112 KiB of KV per token — and 9,216 tokens is what fits. /context then reports context length 9216.

docs.title: How the number is computed
docs.text:
1. Profile the model. /api/show's GGUF metadata supplies the per-layer KV geometry — key/value head counts, sliding-window settings, MLA's compressed latent, recurrent ssm.* state — plus the architecture and parameter count; /api/tags supplies the on-disk size and quantization. The two are cross-checked (params × bytes/param), and the weights split into token embeddings, output layer and blocks instead of being treated as one lump (the report's last line).
  2. Measure the machine. Free VRAM from nvidia-smi — locally, or over one ssh probe for a --remote target.
  3. Subtract the fit margin. max_gpu_margin_mb (default 1 GiB) is llama.cpp's own allowance for projected buffers; max_gpu_overhead_mb (default 0) adds an extra reserve if your stack needs one.
  4. Credit residents. Other loaded models' VRAM is counted back in — it returns when they reload at the new context.
  5. Honor a pinned placement. With /gpu-layers set, the output layer and the topmost blocks are counted as offloaded, not the whole model.

The result is the largest context whose KV cache plus weights fit in the usable VRAM.

docs.title: Verifying with a probe
docs.text: The report ends by saying so: this is an estimate. --probe loads the model at candidate contexts, reads the real GPU split from /api/ps, solves the measured bytes-per-token line and leaves the model warm at the largest 100%-GPU context. See Probes and calibration.

docs.title: Configuration and CLI forms
docs.text:
Knob Default Meaning max_gpu_margin_mb 1024 llama.cpp's fit margin, subtracted from free VRAM. max_gpu_overhead_mb 0 Extra reserve beyond the margin. max_gpu_probes 10 Load attempts a probe may spend.

CLI: --num-ctx max-gpu (with --probe to verify). The result is stored on the session and wins over a raw num_ctx option — and a pinned /gpu-layers is respected when the layers are counted.

If the estimate can't be trusted (no GPU probe available, exotic metadata), the command says so instead of inventing a number; /num-ctx N remains the fallback, and the CPU fit is the other direction.

docs.title: num-ctx
docs.text:
/num-ctx N sets the session's context window; --num-ctx N does it for a run. The value is capped to the model's trained maximum with a warning:

qwen3:0.6b › /num-ctx 8192
num_ctx set to 8192
qwen3:0.6b › /num-ctx 99999999
99999999 exceeds qwen3:0.6b's max context (40960) — capped to 40960
num_ctx set to 40960

The maximum comes from /api/show's model metadata and is cached per model for the run. After the change the resident model is reloaded on the next request — the window is a load-time property, not a per-request one.

docs.title: The two fit forms
docs.text:
/num-ctx also accepts the calculated forms, which pick the number for you:

Form Picks --max-gpu The largest context that keeps the model fully on the GPU (details). --max-cpu N The largest context where the model's host RAM fills N% of available DRAM (details). Either with --probe Same, but verified by actually loading the model (details).

The CLI mirrors them: --num-ctx max-gpu, --num-ctx --max-cpu N, and --probe as a modifier.

docs.title: What "effective" means
docs.text:
The session value is the first of, in order: session num_ctx → the loaded runner's window from /api/ps → the model's default from /api/show. Setting num_ctx here is therefore authoritative until you change it; the /context table and the footer counter always show which window is really in force.

qwen3:0.6b › /context
│ context length │ 9216 │

The raw option is not the managed path. /set parameter num_ctx 8192 does land in the request's options, but it skips the cap warning, the reload coordination and the effective-window bookkeeping — prefer /num-ctx.

docs.title: Context and placement
docs.text: Two numbers decide how a model runs: the context window (how much conversation it can hold) and its GPU placement (how many layers run on the GPU versus the CPU). Ollama picks both automatically; this section is about overriding them deliberately — and about the tools that calculate what the machine can actually afford.

docs.title: The managed knobs
docs.text:
Knob Command / flag What it sets Window size /num-ctx N, --num-ctx N The session's num_ctx, capped to the model's trained maximum. Largest GPU window /num-ctx --max-gpu, --num-ctx max-gpu Estimates the largest context that keeps the model fully on the GPU. DRAM fill /num-ctx --max-cpu N, --num-ctx --max-cpu N Raises the window until the model's host RAM fills N% of available DRAM. Verification --probe on either Loads the model at candidate contexts and reads the real split back. Layer split /gpu-layers SPEC, --gpu-layers SPEC Pins how many layers run on the GPU (N, P%, +N/-N, all, cpu, auto).

Everything is stored on the session, so /load restores it, and it wins over the equivalent raw options (/set parameter num_ctx / num_gpu).

docs.title: Seeing where you stand
docs.text:
/context reports the working numbers:

qwen3:0.6b › /context
             context
╭────────────────────────┬───────╮
│ field                  │ value │
├────────────────────────┼───────┤
│ messages               │     0 │
│ last prompt tokens     │     ? │
│ last completion tokens │     ? │
│ context used           │     ? │
│ context length         │  8192 │
╰────────────────────────┴───────╯

context length is the effective window, resolved in this order: the session's num_ctx → the loaded runner's window (/api/ps) → the model's default (/api/show). The same value feeds the footer's ctx counter and the warning below.

docs.title: The 80% warning, and 85% compaction
docs.text:
When context used / context length reaches 80%, the REPL prints:

context 13112/16384 tokens (80%) — /summarize to compact

and compaction takes over from there — manually with /summarize, or automatically at 85% when config auto_compact is "auto". The same warning runs headlessly at turn start for the agent API, where it is a turn.warning event.

docs.title: Where each piece lives
docs.text:
• num-ctx — setting the window, and the cap.
  • max-gpu / max-cpu — the two fits, with real reports from a 4 GB GPU.
  • Probes and calibration — verifying by loading, and the measured-data cache.
  • GPU layers — the placement spec.
  • Compaction — keeping long sessions inside the window.

docs.title: Probes and calibration
docs.text:
The two fits (max-gpu, max-cpu) are estimates: they combine the model profile with machine numbers but never load anything. --probe is the verification pass — load the model at candidate contexts, read what the machine actually reported, and pick from measurements instead of arithmetic.

smollm2:360m › /num-ctx --max-gpu --probe
probe 1: smollm2:360m at num_ctx 8,192…
          context fit · smollm2:360m on this machine
╭────────────┬────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ model      │ 0.36B params · F16 · llama · 692.0 MiB         │
│ gpu memory │ 1.0 GiB free + 2.8 GiB resident → 3.8 GiB pool │
│ margin     │ 1.0 GiB per device → 2.8 GiB usable            │
│ weights    │ 692.0 MiB                                      │
│ kv cache   │ 40.0 KiB per token · 320.0 MiB at 8,192        │
│ model max  │ 8,192 tokens                                   │
╰────────────┴────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
· crediting smollm2:360m (215.5 MiB on the GPU) — it reloads at the new context and releases that memory
· crediting llama3.2:3b (2.6 GiB on the GPU) — it reloads at the new context and releases that memory
num_ctx 8,192 (capped by the model's max context)
               context probe · smollm2:360m
╭─────────┬───────────┬───────────┬─────┬─────────────────╮
│ num_ctx │      size │      vram │ gpu │ result          │
├─────────┼───────────┼───────────┼─────┼─────────────────┤
│   8,192 │ 633.8 MiB │ 215.5 MiB │ 34% │ partial offload │
╰─────────┴───────────┴───────────┴─────┴─────────────────╯
no probed context stayed fully on the GPU (best 34% at num_ctx 8,192)

That run also shows the honest side of probing: the estimate assumed the two resident models would be evicted on reload and credited their VRAM back, but the probe loaded while they were still resident, so the model only got 34% of its layers onto the GPU. The probe reports what happened instead of the estimate's assumption.

What each probe does:

  1. Load the model at one candidate context (/api/chat with the candidate num_ctx and a tiny generation, keep_alive from the session).
  2. Read back the real split — /api/ps reports the bytes on the GPU vs the rest, for the running model.
  3. Solve the line. A model's footprint is affine in the context size: bytes = weights + kv_per_token × ctx. Two measured points are enough to solve for the slope; the fit then computes the capacity directly instead of bisecting the candidate range.
  4. Finish warm. For --max-gpu the model is left loaded at the largest 100%-GPU context; for --max-cpu never above the requested target.

docs.title: When the estimate and the probe disagree
docs.text:
The estimate can be conservative — the fit margin is deliberately generous. If the estimate declares a context infeasible but a probe might still make it, the command says so and keeps probing:

probing anyway — the estimate's buffers may be conservative

max_gpu_probes / max_cpu_probes (default 10 each) bound how many loads a probe run may spend. A probe that cannot find a feasible context leaves the session untouched and reports the reason instead of guessing.

docs.title: Calibration
docs.text:
Every good measurement — probe results and ordinary resident-model readings — is recorded in a bounded cache at ~/etc/data/ollamarun/ctxfit-calibration.json:

  • Scoped to the model digest, host, hardware, placement and KV settings, so data never leaks between machines or configurations.
  • Expires after 180 days; incompatible or stale data is ignored, never trusted blindly.
  • Feeds back: later estimates start from the measured slope (the fit report says calibrated from N measured context point(s)) and probe searches start near the previous answer, so the second run is faster than the first.

The profile formula remains the fallback whenever the cache is empty — the calibration changes how confident the number is, not whether you get one.

docs.title: The same thing over the API
docs.text: POST /v1/agent/fits runs a probe as an asynchronous job (202 + warnings, progress, cancel) and POST /v1/agent/fit the synchronous estimate — see Context fits. Turn settings.num_ctx: "max-gpu"|"max-cpu" always estimates (never a blocking probe) and reports the result as a session.fit event.

docs.title: Embeddings
docs.text:
Paste a prompt and a model that advertises the embedding capability takes the embeddings route instead of chat: the harness calls /api/embed and prints a summary of the vectors rather than a completion.

$ ollamarun nomic-embed-text "hello world"
       embedding ·
     nomic-embed-text
╭────────────┬───────────╮
│ field      │     value │
├────────────┼───────────┤
│ vectors    │         1 │
│ dimensions │       768 │
│ truncate   │      true │
│ min        │ -0.171560 │
│ max        │  0.122126 │
│ mean       │  0.000305 │
╰────────────┴───────────╯
first 8: [-0.0067, -0.0013, -0.1716, +0.0084, +0.0058, +0.0698, -0.0002,
-0.0431, …]

The table is identity and sanity data (count, dimension, range), with the first few components of the first vector; the full vectors are what the API serves — see Embeddings API.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
Flag Effect --dimensions N Truncate the output vectors to N (models that support it). --truncate [bool] Inputs longer than the context window: true (default) truncates, --truncate=false errors instead. 
$ ollamarun --dimensions 8 nomic-embed-text "hello world"
│ vectors    │         1 │
│ dimensions │         8 │
│ truncate   │      true │

Both are ollama-compatible flags; on a non-embedding model they are ignored with a warning (--dimensions/--truncate only apply to embedding models; ignored). Embedding models need a prompt — an interactive run with one reports embedding models need a prompt (or stdin) and exits 2, so use a one-shot or pipe the text.

docs.title: Detection and lifecycle
docs.text:
The capability comes from /api/show's capabilities list; older servers without it fall back to family-name hints (bert, nomic-embed, …). Embedding models are never unloaded by the harness's housekeeping — the tiny cost of keeping an embedder warm is worth more than reloading it on every request — and the API applies its own embedding capability gate to POST /v1/embeddings (see the API page).

  • Parameters — where the rest of a request's knobs live.
  • Model picker — embedders sort and list like any model.

docs.title: Load, unload and residency
docs.text:
Ollama loads a model on the first request and keeps it for a while (keep_alive); the harness manages that lifecycle so you are not guessing what is resident. /ps is always the source of truth:

llama3.2:3b › /ps
                                ollama ps
╭─────────────────┬───────────┬──────────┬────────┬─────────────────────╮
│ model           │ size      │ VRAM     │ quant  │ until               │
├─────────────────┼───────────┼──────────┼────────┼─────────────────────┤
│ llama3.2:3b     │ 3.2 GiB   │ 2.7 GiB  │ Q4_K_M │ 2026-10-18 12:51:04 │
╰─────────────────┴───────────┴──────────┴────────┴─────────────────────╯

docs.title: Loading
docs.text: The session's model starts loading in the background the moment the REPL opens, and a one-time ollama ps table prints when it becomes resident — so the first message does not wait for a cold load you could have seen coming. One-shots load on demand; either way the timings footer reports the load component per request.

docs.title: Switching
docs.text:
/model NAME and /load --model NAME unload the current model first, then the new one loads lazily:

llama3.2:3b › /model qwen3:0.6b
unloaded llama3.2:3b
qwen3:0.6b ›

/load SESSION is smarter: the saved session carries its own model, so when it differs from the current one the harness asks which to run (current or last, defaulting to the session's) and unloads on the switch. Resuming a session also reconnects to the machine it last ran on.

docs.title: Unloading
docs.text:
Situation Behavior Leaving the REPL (/bye, Ctrl+D) Unloads the session model when config unload_on_exit is true (the default). --keep-loaded Never unloads on exit. --unload Also unloads after a one-shot run. Embedding models Never unloaded — the harness leaves them resident on purpose. ollamarun serve shutdown Unloads only the models that server used, unless --keep-loaded (see [API lifecycle(../../api/index.md#lifecycle)).

The exit unload is visible and verifiable:

llama3.2:3b › /bye
unloaded llama3.2:3b
session 20261018-124236-e402 saved · ~/etc/data/ollamarun/sessions

(--keep-loaded leaves both the model and that line out.)

docs.title: Keep-alive
docs.text:
--keepalive DURATION (preferred: config keepalive) sets how long Ollama keeps the model after a request — 5m, 2h, 0 to unload right after — and it is stored per session, so the until column in /ps reflects it (/params shows the current value under keep_alive).

The unload happens through keep_alive: 0 requests against /api/ps residency checks, never by killing anything — a model unloaded here behaves exactly like one that expired on its own.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Everything a request sends to Ollama beyond the messages: the model options (temperature, num_predict, top_p, …), the system prompt, the thinking flag, keep-alive and the response format. They live on the session and are visible in one table.

docs.title: /params
docs.text:
llama3.2:3b › /params
              session parameters
╭─────────────┬──────────────────────────────╮
│ parameter   │ value                        │
├─────────────┼──────────────────────────────┤
│ temperature │ 0.2                          │
│ num_predict │ 64                           │
│ think       │ None                         │
│ keep_alive  │ 2h                           │
│ gpu layers  │ auto (ollama decides)        │
│ format      │                              │
│ system      │ built-in default (258 chars) │
╰─────────────┴──────────────────────────────╯

Model options appear first (only the ones set), then the session-level knobs: think, keep_alive, gpu layers, format, system.

docs.title: Setting them
docs.text:
Where How REPL /set parameter NAME VALUE — values are coerced (0.2 → float, true → bool, JSON passes through). REPL /set parameter NAME with no value clears it. REPL /set system TEXT — the system prompt (see Prompts). Launch --option NAME=VALUE (repeatable) or --options-json '{"temperature": 0.7}'. Launch --system TEXT, --system-file FILE, --no-system. 
llama3.2:3b › /set parameter temperature 0.2
set temperature = 0.2
llama3.2:3b › /set parameter num_predict 64
set num_predict = 64

Options are passed through to Ollama's /api/chat options object as-is — the same names the API and ollama run --option use. A few interact with dedicated commands and settings:

  • num_gpu — /gpu-layers wins over it in the payload.
  • num_ctx — /num-ctx is the managed path; setting the option directly works but skips the cap/warning logic.
  • think — prefer /think or --think, which also drive the display side.
  • keep_alive — prefer --keepalive/config keepalive; it is stored as the session's keepalive and shown as keep_alive in the table.

docs.title: What a request carries
docs.text: /params is a view of the session; the wire payload is assembled per round by build_payload(): model, messages (history + the effective system message), stream, options, think, keep_alive, format — and the tool schemas when tools are on. Everything in the table above is part of it, except gpu layers, which resolves into options.num_gpu per the /gpu-layers spec.

docs.title: Picker and sorting
docs.text:
A model-less run opens the picker; /model opens it from inside a session. It is a sortable table: type a number, a name, a --sort KEY, or q to quit.

                                                         models
╭────┬───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┬────────────┬─────────┬─────────────────────┬────────────╮
│  # │ name                                                  │       size │  params │ modified            │ family     │
├────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼────────────┼─────────┼─────────────────────┼────────────┤
│  1 │ gpuCurator:latest                                     │    6.1 GiB │    9.7B │ 2026-10-18 10:35:03 │ qwen35     │
│  2 │ d1:3b                                                 │    3.5 GiB │    2.7B │ 2026-10-17 03:56:52 │ lfm2       │
│  3 │ llama3.2:3b-instruct-q8_0                             │    3.2 GiB │    3.2B │ 2026-10-15 10:56:22 │ llama      │
│  4 │ llama3.2:3b                                           │    1.9 GiB │    3.2B │ 2026-10-15 10:56:22 │ llama      │
│  5 │ smollm2:1.7b                                          │    1.7 GiB │    1.7B │ 2026-10-14 12:42:04 │ llama      │
…
model number, name, --sort KEY or 'q' to quit (q):

Quitting without a choice is not an error — but a model-less run then has nothing to do:

model number, name, --sort KEY or 'q' to quit (q): q
no model given — pass MODEL or configure one

docs.title: Sorting
docs.text:
Key Order modified (default) Newest first. name Alphabetical. size Largest first. parameters Most parameters first (MoE totals included). context Largest context window first.

Aliases like recent, newest and mtime map to modified. context costs one lazy /api/show per model, fetched in parallel behind a status line and cached per host — the first sorted-by-context prompt takes a moment, later ones do not.

Ways in: --sort KEY seeds the picker at launch, the picker prompt itself takes --sort KEY in place, and the session remembers the last choice for the next run.

docs.title: From the REPL
docs.text:
/model alone opens the picker; the rest are table views:

llama3.2:3b › /model --list --sort size
                                                    models · by size
╭────┬───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┬────────────┬─────────┬─────────────────────┬────────────╮
│  # │ name                                                  │       size │  params │ modified            │ family     │
├────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼────────────┼─────────┼─────────────────────┼────────────┤
…
Command Effect /model NAME Switch model (unloads the previous one — see Housekeeping). /model --list [--sort KEY] The table without the interactive prompt. /ps The resident models — ollama ps with VRAM, quant and unload time. 
llama3.2:3b › /ps
                                ollama ps
╭─────────────────┬───────────┬──────────┬────────┬─────────────────────╮
│ model           │ size      │ VRAM     │ quant  │ until               │
├─────────────────┼───────────┼──────────┼────────┼─────────────────────┤
│ llama3.2:3b     │ 3.2 GiB   │ 2.7 GiB  │ Q4_K_M │ 2026-10-18 12:51:04 │
╰─────────────────┴───────────┴──────────┴────────┴─────────────────────╯

Tab-completion offers model names at /model in both front ends, and the same table is what pulling falls back to when you decline a pull.

docs.title: Pulling models
docs.text: When the model you asked for is not installed on the target machine, the run does not fail with a bare error. It reports where it looked, probes the free disk space, and offers to pull — with live per-layer progress.

docs.title: The missing-model flow
docs.text:
model nonexistent-model:99b is not installed on 100.102.94.44:11434
free disk space on 100.102.94.44:11434: unknown
pull nonexistent-model:99b? [y/n] (n):
  • y pulls it (/api/pull, one progress bar per layer) and the run continues.
  • n (the default) opens the model picker to choose something that is installed.
  • --pull skips the question and pulls without asking — the shape for scripts and one-shots.
  • /pull [MODEL] does the same from inside the REPL.

The disk line is the machine that will store the model: a local run reports its own numbers (free disk space on this machine: 62.7 GiB of 467.3 GiB (/usr/share/ollama/.ollama/models)), and a remote target is probed with a BatchMode ssh df — reading OLLAMA_MODELS from the ollama unit — which degrades to unknown when ssh cannot answer.

docs.title: --pull
docs.text:
$ ollamarun --no-tools --pull qwen2:0.5b "Reply with exactly: pong"
model qwen2:0.5b is not installed on 127.0.0.1:11434
free disk space on this machine: 92.9 GiB of 467.3 GiB (/usr/share/ollama/.ollama/models)
pulling qwen2:0.5b ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ 352.2 MB / 352.2 MB  94 MB/s  0:00:04
…

Each layer reports its own bytes and rate (Ollama's progress events, one rich bar per layer), then the model load and the answer follow. The check above ran end to end in ~14 s on a LAN, and the model was removed again with the API afterwards.

docs.title: /pull — pull or update
docs.text:
/pull works on installed models too: it checks the manifest and re-verifies every layer, downloading only what changed.

llama3.2:3b › /pull llama3.2:3b
free disk space on http://100.102.94.44:11434: unknown
llama3.2:3b is installed — checking for updates
pulling llama3.2:3b · pulling manifest  ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ 0/? bytes
  dde5aa3fc5ff  ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ 2.0/2.0 GB  0:00:00
  966de95ca8a6  ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ 1.4/1.4 kB  0:00:00
…

With no argument it pulls the session's model.

docs.title: Where models come from
docs.text:
Pulls go to the Ollama server the session talks to — locally or on the --remote machine; there is no separate remote path. The model store is the server's (/usr/share/ollama/.ollama/models by default, OLLAMA_MODELS overrides). Sessions store only the name, so a model pulled here is usable from every front end and the API at once.

  • Housekeeping — what happens to a pulled model when you switch away or exit.
  • [Models API(../../api/openai/models.md) — the same list over HTTP.

docs.title: Footer
docs.text: Two lines of live feedback sit around an answer: the tok/s + context footer while it streams, and the ⏱ timings line under it when it finishes.

docs.title: Live tok/s and context
docs.text:
~20.0 tok/s · (avg 20.9) · 48 tok · ctx 12.345k/32.768k (38.123%)
Segment Meaning ~20.0 tok/s The rate over a 5-second sliding window (TpsEstimator), so it reacts quickly to speed changes. (avg 20.9) The cumulative average for the response. 48 tok Tokens streamed so far this response (thinking counts). ctx 12.345k/32.768k (38.123%) Context the next request will carry over the effective window.

Counting rules: values read raw below 1k, 3-decimal k above. The ctx part appears from the second round on, when there is a base to count from — it adds the current round's chunks to the last request's totals.

The denominator is the window the model is actually loaded with, not the model's architectural maximum: a session num_ctx wins, then the loaded runner's /api/ps window, then the model default. Until the runner reports, the counter is marked provisional. (That resolution order is the same one /context and the 80%/85% warnings use.)

--no-tps hides the footer for a run; /tps [on|off] toggles it mid-session; config tps_footer: false turns it off permanently. The deprecated TUI shows the same numbers in its status bar.

docs.title: Timings
docs.text:
When a response ends on a terminal, a dim line prints under it:

⏱  load 3 ms · prompt 87 tok (1030 tok/s) · eval 2 tok (21.3 tok/s) · total 184 ms
Segment Meaning load Time Ollama spent loading the model (0 when warm). prompt Prompt tokens and their processing rate; cached shows reused KV. eval Generated tokens and their rate. total The whole request.

Visibility rules:

  • On a terminal it is always shown — --verbose is obsolete there and only matters off a terminal.
  • Piped/redirected output omits it unless --verbose:
$ ollamarun --no-tools llama3.2:3b "Reply with exactly: pong"
llama3.2:3b ›
pong
$ ollamarun --no-tools --verbose llama3.2:3b "Reply with exactly: pong"
llama3.2:3b ›
pong
⏱  load 3 ms · prompt 87 tok (1030 tok/s) · eval 2 tok (21.3 tok/s) · total 184 ms
  • --raw and --json never carry it.
  • Config show_stats: false turns it off everywhere.

The same line is what --show prints at the end of a transcript replay (with the session's totals instead of one request's).

docs.title: Streaming markdown
docs.text: Responses stream through a rich.Live view that re-renders the markdown as tokens arrive — headings, lists, tables, code fences and display math all appear already formatted while the model is still writing.

docs.title: Modes
docs.text:
--render What you see When auto (default) markdown on a terminal, plain when piped — markdown Styled markdown, math converted; degrades to plain off-terminal Interactive use plain The text as the model wrote it (still through the live view) When you want no markup interpretation raw Only the answer text on stdout, nothing else Scripts — equivalent to --raw 
$ ollamarun --no-tools --render raw llama3.2:3b "Reply with exactly: pong"
pong

/render [markdown|plain|raw] switches mid-session; /render alone shows the current mode. --raw is the same as --render raw.

docs.title: While it streams
docs.text:
The view refreshes on a throttle, not per token — content stays readable and the terminal is not redrawn hundreds of times a second. Two knobs matter:

  • max_render_chars (config, default 12000): past this much content in one response, the renderer switches to raw streaming — the answer keeps arriving, it just stops re-parsing the markdown for speed.
  • --nowordwrap: don't wrap long lines to the terminal width.
  • --pager buffers the whole response and opens it in $PAGER when done — see Pager.

The user message is framed in a small right-aligned box, the model's answer flows under a rule, and a tool loop's final answer gets a centered response divider (tool panels are their own boxes — see The tool loop).

docs.title: Off a terminal
docs.text:
Piped and redirected output is always plain: the live view needs a terminal, so markdown itself degrades to plain there. The response text is still written line by line as it arrives. For machine output, --raw/--json skip the presentation entirely — see Usage.

  • 2D math — what the display-math renderer does.
  • Thinking panel — the collapsible reasoning view.
  • Footer — the tok/s and ctx line under the answer.

docs.title: 2D math
docs.text:
Display math is not printed as LaTeX. A self-contained parser and layout engine (ollamarun_lib/mathrender.py) turns it into 2D Unicode art — stacked fractions, radical overlines, limits above and below big operators — centered in cyan. Inline math is flattened to a single line instead.

The engine handles display math written as $$…$$ or \[…\] on its own line(s); math inside a sentence, list item or table cell goes through the inline path so it stays inside its block.

docs.title: What it renders
docs.text:
Real output from the engine (the text here; it is centered and cyan on a terminal):

LaTeX Rendered as \frac{a+b}{2} A stacked fraction with a rule. \sqrt{x^2+y^2} A radical with an overline. \sum_{i=1}^{n} … ∑ with limits above and below. \int_0^\infty … ∫₀^∞, tight side limits. \lim_{x \to 0} … lim with x → 0 beneath. \begin{pmatrix} … \end{pmatrix} A parenthesised matrix. \begin{cases} … \end{cases} A brace with stacked cases. \boxed{E = mc^2} A rounded box. \binom{n}{k} Binomial in big parentheses. \vec{v}\cdot\hat{n} + \bar{x} Accents above the letters.

Verbatim, as the layout engine returns them:

\frac{a+b}{2}
   a + b
   ─────
     2

\sqrt{x^2+y^2}
   ───────
   √x² + y²

\sum_{i=1}^{n} i = \frac{n(n+1)}{2}
     n       n(n + 1)
     ∑   i = ────────
   i = 1        2

\lim_{x \to 0} \frac{\sin x}{x} = 1
         sin x
    lim  ───── = 1
   x → 0   x

\begin{pmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{pmatrix}
   ⎛ a  b ⎞
   ⎝ c  d ⎠

\begin{cases} x & x>0 \\ -x & x\le 0 \end{cases}
   ⎧ x  x > 0
   ⎩ -x  x ≤ 0

\begin{aligned} a &= b+c \\ d &= e \end{aligned}
   a = b + c
   d = e

\boxed{E = mc^2}
   ╭─────────╮
   │ E = mc² │
   ╰─────────╯

\binom{n}{k} = \frac{n!}{k!(n-k)!}
   ⎛n⎞       n!
   ⎜ ⎟ = ──────────
   ⎝k⎠   k!(n - k)!

\mathbb{R} \subset \mathbb{C}, \; \mathcal{L}
   ℝ ⊂ ℂ,  ℒ

\alpha + \beta = \gamma \ne \delta \approx \epsilon
   α + β = γ ≠ δ ≈ ε

Accents (\vec, \hat, \bar), Greek letters, \mathbb/\mathcal, \left…\right delimiters, sub/superscripts (stacked for big operators, raised otherwise) and \,-style spacing come along too.

docs.title: Inline math
docs.text: $x^2 + y_i$ → x² + yᵢ; $\alpha\beta$ → αβ; $\frac{1}{2}$ → 1/2. Inline conversion is line-based, so it stays safe inside tables and sentences.

docs.title: Fallbacks, not crashes
docs.text:
Anything the layout engine cannot lay out — an unknown environment, an unknown macro, a formula too wide for the terminal, an internal over-budget — falls back to the pylatexenc flattening path and is shown literally instead of half-rendered:

$$ \begin{foo} x + 1 \end{foo} $$     →     x + 1      (literal block)
$$ \notacommand{x} $$                 →     x          (literal block)

Nothing unsupported ever takes the rendering down; the expression is reproduced as best it can be.

docs.title: Live example
docs.text:
Asked to repeat a formula exactly, the model's answer is laid out by the engine on the way in:

$ ollamarun --no-tools llama3.2:3b "Repeat this exact line, with no extra text: \$\$e^{i\pi} + 1 = 0\$\$"
llama3.2:3b ›
                            e^(iπ) + 1 = 0

The same run with --no-math shows the source instead:

$$e^{i\pi} + 1 = 0$$

/math [on|off] toggles conversion mid-session; --no-math is the per-run flag. Conversion runs in the renderer's markdown path, so it applies to live streaming, transcript replays and HTML exports alike.

docs.title: Thinking panel
docs.text: Reasoning models stream their thinking alongside the answer. The harness shows it live but collapsed, so it never buries the answer you asked for.

docs.title: The collapsed line
docs.text:
While the model thinks, a single animated line ticks in place:

⠋  thinking · 161 chars · Ctrl+T to expand

The count grows as tokens arrive. When the answer starts, the line stays put (the thinking is kept, just folded) and the response streams under it.

docs.title: Ctrl+T, and the three modes
docs.text:
Ctrl+T expands the panel in place — a boxed, dim, markdown-rendered preview capped to the terminal's height — and pressing it again collapses it. The stream never pauses for either.

Start mode Where Effect collapsed config thinking (default) The ticking line. expanded --show-thinking, config The panel starts open. hidden --hidethinking, config Thinking is not shown at all.

/thinking [show|collapse|hide|toggle|full] covers them from inside a session — and full prints the whole stored reasoning after the fact, no terminal-height cap:

qwen3:1.7b › /thinking full
│ Okay, the user is asking for a two-item markdown bullet list of primary
│ colors. Let me think. The primary colors in painting are typically red
│ and blue, but wait, in light theory, it's red, green, and blue. …

The thinking is stored on the assistant message either way (session JSON, exports and --show include it), so hiding it never loses it.

docs.title: /think is a different knob
docs.text:
Easy to mix up:

  • /think [on|off|low|medium|high] — whether the model thinks at all (sent as Ollama's think parameter).
  • /thinking [mode] — how the thinking is displayed.

--think STR is the launch flag for the former; the config key thinking is the display mode.

docs.title: Off a terminal
docs.text: Piped and redirected runs print the thinking text plainly before the answer (no live panel exists there); --hidethinking removes it. --json carries it in message.thinking. The API surface exposes reasoning models as delta.reasoning_content on the OpenAI side — see [Streaming(../../api/openai/streaming.md).

docs.title: Transcript replay
docs.text:
ollamarun --show ID replays a saved conversation the way it looked live: the title rule and metadata line, the user's boxes, the model's rendered answers (markdown and math), the tool call and result panels with their colours, expanded thinking panels, image markers, cancelled notes, the system prompt when the session has one — and a stats line at the end.

$ ollamarun --show 20261018-113558-13ec
────────── Use write_file to write the text hello-from-the-model to /t… ──────────
id 20261018-113558-13ec · model llama3.2:3b · created 2026-10-18 11:35:58 ·
updated 2026-10-18 11:37:11 · 4 messages
        ╭──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── you ─╮
        │ Use write_file to write the text hello-from-the-model to             │
        │ /tmp/olladocs-demo.txt. Then confirm you did it.                     │
        ╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
╭─ tool · write_file ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ { "append": false, "content": "hello-from-the-model",                        │
│   "path": "/tmp/olladocs-demo.txt" }                                         │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
╭─ tool · write_file · ok ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ wrote 20 chars to /tmp/olladocs-demo.txt                                     │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
The written text is indeed "hello-from-the-model" and its length is 20 characters.
1 turns · 2937 prompt tok · 51 completion tok · 71s total

It is not a re-run: everything comes from the session file. That is what makes the store the conversation's record — thinking, tool arguments, tool results, approvals and settings are all still there weeks later. (This is also why Storage says the JSON files, not the index, are the truth.)

--show takes any unique id prefix or session reference; find one with --list or --search, the /sessions picker in the REPL, or -r at launch. For how replays are put together under the hood, the pipeline is renderer.render_transcript() reading the same panels the live view used — see Architecture.

Note

In the REPL, /show [topic] is a different thing: it prints model details (info, license, modelfile, parameters, system, template), mirroring ollama show. Transcript replay is the CLI's --show ID, plus the browser in /sessions.

docs.title: Branching
docs.text:
/branch [TITLE] forks the conversation into a new session, leaving the current one untouched — the safe way to explore a different direction without losing the path you were on.

llama3.2:3b › /branch side quest
branched 20261018-122252-de60

The current session is saved first, then the branch is created as a full copy and becomes the active session. Everything conversational and behavioral comes along:

  • all messages so far (the branch starts with the same history),
  • system, parameters, think, keepalive, format, gpu_layers,
  • tags, stats, the approval tool_allow fingerprints and tool_rules,
  • tools_disabled and the tts settings.

What it does not copy: the title (unless you pass one, it becomes <original title> (branch)) and the id — the branch is an independent session from the moment it is created, so future turns on either side never interfere.

Typical uses:

  • Try an alternative. Branch, then /retry or /edit on the branch; the original stays exactly as it was.
  • Fork at a decision point. Get a file to a working state, branch, and keep one line of work "clean" while you experiment.
  • Split a long session into per-topic children before the context gets tight.

Going back is ordinary session work: /sessions (or -c/--session/ --show from the CLI) lists both, and the original is one pick away. The prompt column in /sessions shows the title, so (branch) children are easy to spot.

See Search and export for finding a parent again by content, and Save and load for resuming options.

docs.title: Save and load
docs.text: Every interactive session and every one-shot (unless --no-save) lands in the store, and any of them can be picked back up — from the command line or from inside the REPL.

docs.title: Resuming from the command line
docs.text:
Form Meaning -c [ID], --continue [ID] Continue the most recent session, or the given one. -r, --resume Browse saved sessions and pick one. --session NAME Continue the session named NAME, or create it. --new Force a fresh session even with -c/--session.

A named session keeps its name as its title, and later runs can omit the model — it comes from the session:

$ ollamarun --no-tools --session demo llama3.2:3b "Remember the number 41. Reply with OK only."
OK
$ ollamarun --no-tools --session demo "What number did I ask you to remember? Answer with the number only."
41

-c continues the most recently updated session, with its model:

$ ollamarun --no-tools -c "Now add one to that number. Answer with the number only."
42

-c and similar prompts

Because stored titles are derived from prompts, a prompt that matches an existing title can be mistaken for a session reference by -c and get swallowed (the run then reports no prompt). Reusing prompt wording is the trigger; --session or --continue ID avoids it. Tracked as issue #44.

-r opens the same browser as /sessions: a table where you type a number, an id, a filter to narrow, or q to quit.

Resuming also reconnects to the machine the session last ran on, unless --host/--remote override it — see Remote.

docs.title: /load and switching
docs.text:
• /load SESSION resumes a saved session; when its model differs from the current one the harness asks which model to run and unloads the current one before switching.
  • /load MODEL (or /model NAME) switches the model instead, unloading the previous resident unless it is an embedding model.

docs.title: Saving a model out of a session
docs.text:
/save NAME bakes the current conversation into an Ollama model, using the session as its messages and the effective system prompt as its SYSTEM — a snapshot you can ollamarun NAME later:

llama3.2:3b › /save olladocs-test:latest
creating olladocs-test:latest from llama3.2:3b…
  using existing layer sha256:dde5aa3fc5ff…
  creating new layer sha256:7b935f8b1107…
  writing manifest
  success
created olladocs-test:latest — `ollamarun olladocs-test:latest`

(Created model above was removed again with the API's /api/delete after the check.)

docs.title: Starting over
docs.text:
Command Effect /clear Empties the context; keeps settings, keeps the file's identity (context cleared), starts a new id so the old file stays. /new [TITLE] Saves the current session and starts a brand-new one (new session 20261018-122626-02cd). /branch Forks instead of starting over — see Branching.

Both are also reachable by just starting another run with --new or a different --session.

docs.title: Titles and tags
docs.text: Created automatically from the first prompt, settable with --title, --tag, /title and /tag, or asked from the model with --auto-title: see Titles and tags.

docs.title: Search and export
docs.text: Four inspection commands read the store without touching it, all sharing one output convention: a rich table on a terminal, or --json / --csv / --markdown with --out FILE for scripts.

docs.title: --search — inside the messages
docs.text:
$ ollamarun --search color
                                 search: color
╭───────────────┬───────────────┬───────────────┬───────────────┬──────────────╮
│ id            │ title         │ model         │ updated_at    │ match        │
├───────────────┼───────────────┼───────────────┼───────────────┼──────────────┤
│ 20261018-113… │ What color    │ minicpm-v4.6… │ 2026-10-18T1… │ What color   │
│               │ fills the     │               │               │ fills the    │
│               │ attached      │               │               │ attached     │
│               │ image? …      │               │               │ image? …     │
│ 20261018-113… │ Reply with a  │ llama3.2:3b   │ 2026-10-18T1… │ …wo-item     │
│               │ two-item …    │               │               │ markdown …   │
╰───────────────┴───────────────┴───────────────┴───────────────┴──────────────╯

Search covers what is in the session files — including thinking, tool calls and results — since it scans the stored JSON.

docs.title: --show — replay a transcript
docs.text:
$ ollamarun --show 20261018-113558-13ec
────────── Use write_file to write the text hello-from-the-model to /t… ──────────
id 20261018-113558-13ec · model llama3.2:3b · created 2026-10-18 11:35:58 ·
updated 2026-10-18 11:37:11 · 4 messages
        ╭──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── you ─╮
        │ Use write_file to write the text hello-from-the-model to             │
        │ /tmp/olladocs-demo.txt. Then confirm you did it.                     │
        ╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
╭─ tool · write_file ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ { "append": false, "content": "hello-from-the-model",                        │
│   "path": "/tmp/olladocs-demo.txt" }                                         │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
╭─ tool · write_file · ok ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ wrote 20 chars to /tmp/olladocs-demo.txt                                     │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
The written text is indeed "hello-from-the-model" and its length is 20 characters.
1 turns · 2937 prompt tok · 51 completion tok · 71s total

It is the live view's rendering again — boxes, tool panels, colours, thinking — plus a stats line. In the REPL, /show [topic] shows model details (info, license, modelfile, …, ollama-style); the transcript replay is the CLI's --show ID.

docs.title: --export — take a session away
docs.text:
--export ID writes the session out; --export-format md|json|html picks the shape (default md). The markdown export serializes the tool calls as JSON blocks:

# Use write_file to write the text hello-from-the-model to /t…

- **id:** `20261018-113558-13ec`
- **model:** `llama3.2:3b`
- **created:** 2026-10-18T11:35:58.014222-03:00
- **updated:** 2026-10-18T11:37:11.740373-03:00

## User

Use write_file to write the text hello-from-the-model to /tmp/olladocs-demo.txt.
Then confirm you did it.

## Assistant

```json
[{"id": "call_1ftvnkvz", "function": {"name": "write_file",
  "arguments": {"path": "/tmp/olladocs-demo.txt", "content": "hello-from-the-model"}}}]
```

The JSON export is the session file plus the derived presentation fields (title, display_title) — the machine-readable copy. The HTML one renders the same transcript the replay shows into a self-contained styled document (recorder.export_html), which is what --out session.html is for.

Two open issues with the printed forms

  • Printing a machine format to a narrow terminal can wrap long lines (rich printing), which breaks --json/--csv parsing; --out FILE is immune. Tracked as issue #42.
  • --export-format html currently prints the transcript to stdout before the document, even with --out; the file itself is correct. Tracked as issue #43.

docs.title: --reindex
docs.text: --reindex rebuilds index.json from the session files. It is the repair step when the index ever drifts (a manual file copy, a killed process) — sessions themselves are the source of truth.

docs.title: The convention
docs.text:
Flag Effect --json JSON array of records (list/search) or the API payload (chat runs). --csv CSV with the table's columns. --markdown The same table as a markdown pipe table. --out FILE Write the format to a file instead of stdout.

All four commands accept them; without a format flag you get the rich table.

docs.title: Storage
docs.text: Sessions are the durable half of the harness. One conversation is one JSON file plus a shared index — a store, not a cache, and nothing is deleted without going through the trash.

docs.title: Where things live
docs.text:
Path What ~/etc/data/ollamarun/sessions/<id>.json One session file per conversation. ~/etc/data/ollamarun/index.json The list view's index: id, title, model, host, timestamps, counts, tags. ~/etc/data/ollamarun/index.json.lock The flock file guarding index read-modify-write. ~/etc/data/ollamarun/history Prompt input history (unless OLLAMA_NOHISTORY). ~/etc/data/ollamarun/artifacts/ The serve artifact store (Artifacts). ~/etc/data/ollamarun/ctxfit-calibration.json Context-fit measurements (Probes and calibration).

Session ids look like 20261018-122556-a496 (timestamp plus a short random suffix). Anywhere an id is taken — --show, --export, -c, /load — a unique prefix or an unambiguous title reference works, so you rarely type the whole thing.

Field On Meaning thinking assistant The reasoning text a thinking model produced. tool_calls assistant The call array the model asked for. tool_name tool Which tool produced this result. images user Attached images (path/name/sha1/size, base64 when embedded). files user @file mentions that were inlined. cancelled either The turn was interrupted here.

Settings live on the session too: system, parameters, think, keepalive, format, gpu_layers, tools_disabled, the approval tool_allow/tool_rules, and the tts fields — so /load restores the whole working context, not just the chat.

docs.title: Writes are atomic, and the index is locked
docs.text: Saving goes through a temp file named per writer plus os.replace, so an interrupted write can never leave a half session. The index read-modify-write runs under a shared RLock and an exclusive flock on index.json.lock: a CLI saving while ollamarun serve runs cannot lose entries, and --reindex rebuilds the index from the session files if it ever drifts.

docs.title: Deletes go to the trash
docs.text:
--delete ID (asks; -y skips) and the store's delete move the session file to the XDG trash via trash-put — never a raw unlink:

$ ollamarun --delete 20261018-111147-a9d6 -y
trashed 20261018-111147-a9d6

The file is recoverable from ~/.local/share/Trash/ (with a .trashinfo recording where it came from), and --list no longer shows it. In the REPL, /clear empties the context but keeps the session's settings and starts a new id under the same file; /new saves the current session and starts a fresh one.

docs.title: Not every run is saved
docs.text:
--no-save keeps a run out of the store entirely — useful for scripting and for throwaway checks — and --json/--raw runs still respect it. The REPL's prompt history is the only other thing persisted by default, and OLLAMA_NOHISTORY disables that too.

  • Save and load — resuming conversations.
  • Search and export — getting data back out.

docs.title: Titles and tags
docs.text: Every session gets a title and can carry tags; both show up in the /sessions picker and --list, and both survive in the index.

docs.title: Titles
docs.text:
A new session is titled from its first prompt (naive_title() — the first line, trimmed to a sane length). --title TEXT sets one up front, and --auto-title asks the model for a better one via the title prompt:

$ ollamarun --no-tools --auto-title llama3.2:3b "Explain in one sentence what a haiku is."
llama3.2:3b ›
A haiku is a traditional Japanese poetry form consisting of three lines with
a syllable count of 5-7-5, often capturing a moment or image from nature.
$ ollamarun --list
| 20261018-122724-96a7 | Understanding Haiku Poetry Basics | llama3.2:3b | …

In the REPL:

Command Effect /title Show the current title. /title TEXT Set it. /title --auto Ask the model to (re)title from the first message.

The title is also the header of a transcript replay and the first column everywhere sessions are listed. Renaming is cheap — the title lives on the session, not in the filename.

docs.title: Tags
docs.text:
Tags are a free-form list on the session. Set them at launch (--tag is repeatable) or in the REPL:

llama3.2:3b › /tag add demo docs
tags demo, docs
llama3.2:3b › /tag list
tags: demo, docs
llama3.2:3b › /tag rm docs
tags demo

/tag with no argument lists them; add/rm take several at once. Tags appear in --list/--search output and in the exported JSON, which makes them the light-weight way to group work (one tag per project, per machine, per experiment).

docs.title: Names, titles and ids
docs.text:
Three related things, easy to mix up:

  • id — 20261018-122556-a496, system-generated; any unique prefix works as a reference.
  • name — what --session NAME keys on; it is also stored as the title when the session is created that way.
  • title — the display label, derived from the prompt or set by --title//title/--auto-title.

--list shows the title; --show, --export and -c accept ids, id prefixes, names and title references.

docs.title: Undo, retry and edit
docs.text: Three ways to redo the recent past. All of them operate on the last exchange, where an exchange is everything from one user message through the model's answer — tool rounds included, so a turn that called tools goes away as one unit.

docs.title: /undo — drop the last exchange
docs.text:
llama3.2:3b › /undo
undone

The last user message and everything after it are removed, the stats' turn count drops by one, and the session is saved. With an empty history it says nothing to undo.

docs.title: /retry — ask again
docs.text:
llama3.2:3b › /retry
retrying…
llama3.2:3b › Blue

The last user message stays; every assistant/tool message after it is discarded and the request is made again, so you get a fresh sample. Retrying after a cancelled or failed answer is the usual reason.

docs.title: /edit — fix the question
docs.text:
/edit reopens the last user message in $OLLAMA_EDITOR, replaces it with what you save, drops the old answer and regenerates — the scalpel of the three:

llama3.2:3b › Name one color. Answer with one word.
Blue
llama3.2:3b › /edit
resending edited message…
Apple

The editor was prefilled with the original message and returned Name one fruit. Answer with one word.; the exchange was replaced, not appended. An empty editor result cancels (edit cancelled). Full mechanics on the Editor page.

docs.title: Which one?
docs.text:
Goal Command Forget the last exchange and go on /undo Same question, another answer /retry Change the question itself /edit Fork instead of rewriting /branch

All three keep the rest of the conversation (and every setting) intact, and all three are saved immediately — closing the session afterwards does not bring the undone exchange back.

docs.title: Tools
docs.text:
With tools on — the default — every chat request carries the built-in tool definitions, and the model can call them through Ollama function calling. The harness is the difference between a chat that says it listed your files and one that actually did: calls are executed locally behind an approval gate, their results go back to the model as tool messages, and the loop repeats until the model answers without asking for anything else.

  • The tool loop — what happens between a call and the answer.
  • Approvals and policy — the gate and its modes.
  • Definitions — the JSON the model sees, and how to change it.
  • Reference — every tool with its parameters.

docs.title: What the model gets
docs.text:
The request carries one schema per enabled tool, built from the definition files: name, description and JSON-schema parameters. Which tools are offered depends on the host:

Condition Tools Always run_shell, run_python, read_file, write_file, edit_file, list_dir, make_dir, move_file, copy_file, delete_file, fetch_url, search_sessions, list_models, system_status, context_status, session_info The ddgs package resolves web_search A tts-remote CLI resolves speak, list_voices A chemInventoryAPI CLI resolves (config chem_tools: true) chem_search, chem_container, chem_locations ollamarun serve runs an artifact store publish_artifact

Each tool also has aliases for names models tend to invent — /tools search off disables web_search, and a call to curl or mkdir resolves onto the real tool before the registry is searched. /tools NAME help lists a tool's aliases.

docs.title: The four ways a call is handled
docs.text:
1. Auto — read-only tools (read_file, list_dir, …) and the speak tool never ask.
  2. Safe list — allowlisted shell commands (ls, cat, grep, rg, read-only git, …) and provably harmless Python run unattended.
  3. Rules and remembered calls — a generalized rule or an exact remembered call from this session runs without asking.
  4. Ask — everything else asks in the REPL; in an unattended run it is denied with a note, unless -y/--yes or /tools policy auto is in effect.

Details and the prompt itself: Approvals and policy.

docs.text:

│ NAME help                    │ description, parameters (required/optional), aliases │
│ NAME call ARGS               │ run it yourself: call {"query": "x"} · call query=x  │
│ help [NAME]                  │ this reference, or one tool's page                   │
